bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第184卷卷第一百八十四

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 184, Volume One Hundred Eighty-four
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 184

sentences.zh: 【隋紀八】　起強閼赤奮若六月，不滿一年。

translations.literal: [Sui Records 8] Beginning from the sixth month of the year Qiangge Chifenruo, less than one year.
translations.idiomatic: [Sui Records 8] Covering the period from the sixth month of the Qiangge Chifenruo cycle year, less than a full year.

sentences.zh: 六月，己卯，李建成等至晉陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jimao, Li Jiancheng and the others arrived at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day jimao, Li Jiancheng and his party reached Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 劉文靜勸李淵與突厥相結，資其士馬以益兵勢。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing urged Li Yuan to ally with the Turks, relying on their warriors and horses to augment his military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing advised Li Yuan to join forces with the Turks and draw on their cavalry and troops to strengthen his army.

sentences.zh: 淵從之，自為手啟，卑辭厚禮，遺始畢可汗云：「欲大舉義兵，遠迎主上，復與突厥和親，如開皇之時。

translations.literal: Yuan followed this advice, personally drafting a letter in humble language with rich gifts, sending it to Qaghan Shibi, saying: "I wish to raise righteous troops on a grand scale, go far to welcome the sovereign, and restore marital alliance with the Turks as in the Kaihuang era.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan agreed. He wrote a personal letter himself, couched in deferential terms and accompanied by lavish gifts, and sent it to Qaghan Shibi: "I intend to launch a great righteous campaign, go far to welcome the emperor home, and renew the marriage alliance with the Turks as in Emperor Wen's reign.

sentences.zh: 若能與我俱南，願勿侵暴百姓；

translations.literal: If you can march south with me, I hope you will not ravage the common people;
translations.idiomatic: If you will march south with me, I ask that you not harm the common people;

sentences.zh: 若但和親，坐受寶貨，亦唯可汗所擇。

translations.literal: if you wish only for alliance by marriage and to sit and receive treasure, that too is for the qaghan alone to choose."
translations.idiomatic: if you prefer only an alliance and to receive treasure while remaining at home, that too is entirely for the qaghan to decide."

sentences.zh: 」始畢得啟，謂其大臣曰：「隋主為人，我所知也。

translations.literal: Shibi received the letter and said to his ministers: "The character of the Sui ruler—I know it well.
translations.idiomatic: When Shibi received the letter, he told his ministers: "I know the Sui emperor's character well.

sentences.zh: 若迎以來，必害唐公而擊我無疑矣。

translations.literal: If he is welcomed back, he will surely harm Duke Tang and attack us without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: If we bring him back, he will certainly harm Duke Tang and attack us—that is beyond doubt.

sentences.zh: 苟唐公自為天子，我當不避盛暑，以兵馬助之。

translations.literal: If Duke Tang makes himself Son of Heaven, I shall not shrink from the height of summer and shall aid him with troops and horses."
translations.idiomatic: If Duke Tang declares himself emperor, I will not hesitate even in the heat of summer to send troops and horses to help him."

sentences.zh: 」即命以此意為復書。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered a reply drafted in this sense.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered a reply written along these lines.

sentences.zh: 使者七日而返，將佐皆喜，請從突厥之言，淵不可。

translations.literal: The envoy returned in seven days; the generals and aides were all pleased and asked to follow the Turks' proposal, but Yuan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy returned after seven days. The officers were delighted and urged Li Yuan to accept the Turks' offer, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 裴寂、劉文靜等皆曰：「今義兵雖集而戎馬殊乏，胡兵非所須，而馬不可失；

translations.literal: Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing, and the others all said: "Though righteous troops have gathered, war horses are extremely scarce; barbarian soldiers are not what we need, but the horses must not be lost;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji, Liu Wenjing, and the others all said: "Our righteous army has assembled, but we are desperately short of horses. We do not need Turkic infantry, but we cannot let these horses slip away;

sentences.zh: 若復稽回，恐其有悔。

translations.literal: if we delay and turn back again, I fear they may regret it."
translations.idiomatic: if we hesitate any longer, they may change their minds."

sentences.zh: 」淵曰：「諸君宜更思其次。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "You gentlemen should think further of an alternative."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said: "You should all think of another approach."

sentences.zh: 」寂等乃請尊天子為太上皇，立代王為帝，以安隋室；

translations.literal: Ji and the others then asked to honor the Son of Heaven as Retired Emperor, install Prince Dai as emperor, and thereby pacify the house of Sui;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji and the others then proposed honoring the emperor as Retired Emperor, enthroning Prince Dai, and thus preserving the Sui dynasty;

sentences.zh: 移檄郡縣；

translations.literal: issue proclamations to the commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: issue proclamations to the provinces and counties;

sentences.zh: 改易旗幟，雜用絳白，以示突厥。

translations.literal: change the banners and flags, mixing crimson and white, to show this to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: change the army banners to a mix of crimson and white, as a signal to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「此可謂『掩耳盜鐘』，然逼於時事，不得不爾。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "This may be called 'covering one's ears while stealing a bell,' yet compelled by the times, it cannot be otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said: "This is what people call 'covering your ears while stealing the bell'—pure self-deception—but the circumstances leave us no choice.

sentences.zh: 」乃許之，遣使以此議告突厥。

translations.literal: He then consented and sent envoys to inform the Turks of this plan.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed and sent envoys to explain this plan to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 西河郡不從淵命，甲申，淵使建成、世民將兵擊西河；

translations.literal: Xihe commandery did not obey Yuan's orders; on the day jiashen, Yuan sent Jiancheng and Shimin to lead troops against Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: Xihe Commandery refused to obey Li Yuan. On the day jiashen, he sent Jiancheng and Shimin to attack it with an army;

sentences.zh: 命太原令太原溫大有與之偕行，曰：「吾兒年少，以卿參謀軍事；

translations.literal: he ordered the magistrate of Taiyuan, Wen Dayou of Taiyuan, to go with them, saying: "My sons are young; I rely on you to advise on military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the magistrate of Taiyuan, Wen Dayou, to accompany them, saying: "My sons are still young—I appoint you to counsel them in military matters;

sentences.zh: 事之成敗，當以此行卜之。

translations.literal: whether matters succeed or fail shall be divined by this campaign."
translations.idiomatic: whether we succeed or fail will be foretold by this expedition."

sentences.zh: 」時軍士新集，鹹未閱習，建成、世民與之同甘苦，遇敵則以身先之。

translations.literal: At that time the soldiers had only recently assembled and none had yet been drilled; Jiancheng and Shimin shared their hardships, and when they met the enemy they took the lead themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The troops had only just been assembled and had not yet been trained. Jiancheng and Shimin shared their hardships, and when they met the enemy they led from the front.

sentences.zh: 近道菜果，非買不食，軍士有竊之者，輒求其主償之，亦不詰竊者，軍士及民皆感悅。

translations.literal: Along the road were vegetables and fruit; they would not eat what they had not bought. When soldiers stole some, they would seek out the owner to compensate him and would not punish the thief; soldiers and common people alike were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When they passed fruit and vegetables along the road, they would eat only what they had paid for. If a soldier stole something, they made restitution to the owner without punishing the thief. Soldiers and civilians alike were deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 至西河城下，民有欲入城者，皆聽其入。

translations.literal: When they reached Xihe city, any common people who wished to enter the city were allowed to do so.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Xihe, they allowed any civilians who wished to enter the city to go in freely.

sentences.zh: 郡丞高德儒閉城拒守，己丑，攻拔之。

translations.literal: The assistant magistrate Gao Deru closed the city and resisted; on the day jichou, they stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant magistrate Gao Deru shut the gates and held out, but on the day jichou they stormed and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 執德儒至軍門，世民數之曰：「汝指野鳥為鸞，以欺人主，取高官，吾興義兵，正為誅佞人耳！

translations.literal: They seized Deru and brought him to the camp gate; Shimin rebuked him, saying: "You pointed to wild birds and called them phoenixes, deceiving the sovereign to win high office. I have raised righteous troops precisely to execute flatterers like you!
translations.idiomatic: They brought Gao Deru before the camp gate. Shimin denounced him: "You called wild birds phoenixes to deceive the emperor and win high office. I raised this righteous army precisely to execute sycophants like you!

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: He was then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He was then beheaded.

sentences.zh: 自余不戮一人，秋毫無犯，各尉撫使復業，遠近聞之大悅。

translations.literal: Beyond this they executed no one; not the slightest thing was violated; each was comforted and enabled to resume his livelihood; near and far, all who heard of it were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond him they killed no one and harmed nothing. They comforted the people and let them return to their livelihoods. News of this spread far and wide, to universal acclaim.

sentences.zh: 建成等引兵還晉陽，往返凡九日。

translations.literal: Jiancheng and the others led the army back to Jinyang; the round trip took only nine days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and his forces returned to Jinyang—the entire round trip had taken only nine days.

sentences.zh: 淵喜曰：「以此行兵，雖橫行天下可也。

translations.literal: Yuan said with pleasure: "With troops like these, one could march across the world.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said with delight: "With an army like this, you could march anywhere in the realm.

sentences.zh: 」遂定入關之計。

translations.literal: He then settled the plan to enter the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He then fixed on the plan to march into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 淵開倉以賑貧民，應募者日益多。

translations.literal: Yuan opened the granaries to relieve the poor; those who answered the call to arms grew daily more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan opened the granaries to feed the poor, and recruits poured in day by day.

sentences.zh: 淵命為三軍，分左右，通謂之義士。

translations.literal: Yuan ordered them organized into three armies, divided into left and right, collectively called Righteous Warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan organized them into three armies, left and right wings, collectively known as the Righteous Warriors.

sentences.zh: 裴寂等上淵號為大將軍，癸巳，建大將軍府；

translations.literal: Pei Ji and the others submitted the title of Grand General for Yuan; on the day guisi, they established the Grand General's headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji and the others urged Li Yuan to assume the title of Grand General. On the day guisi they established his headquarters;

sentences.zh: 以寂為長史，劉文靜為司馬，唐儉及前長安尉溫大雅為記室，大雅仍與弟大有共掌機密，武士擭為鎧曹，劉政會及武城崔善為、太原張道源為戶曹，晉陽長上邽姜謨為司功參軍，太谷長殷開山為府掾，長孫順德、劉弘基、竇琮及鷹揚郎將高平王長諧、天水姜寶誼、陽屯為左、右統軍；

translations.literal: Ji was made chief clerk, Liu Wenjing marshal, Tang Jian and the former Chang'an commandant Wen Daya recorders; Daya together with his younger brother Dayou jointly managed confidential affairs; Wu Shihuo was armor officer; Liu Zhenghui, Cui Shanwei of Wucheng, and Zhang Daoyuan of Taiyuan were revenue officers; the magistrate of Jinyang, Jiang Mo of Shanggui, was director of merit; the magistrate of Taigu, Yin Kaishan, was headquarters aide; Sun Shunde, Liu Hongji, Dou Cong, and the Yingyang commandant Wang Changxie of Gaoping, Jiang Baoyi of Tianshui, and Yang Tun were left and right army commanders;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji became chief clerk, Liu Wenjing marshal, Tang Jian and the former Chang'an commandant Wen Daya recorders—with Daya and his brother Dayou jointly handling confidential affairs. Wu Shihuo was armor officer; Liu Zhenghui, Cui Shanwei of Wucheng, and Zhang Daoyuan of Taiyuan were revenue officers; Jiang Mo, magistrate of Jinyang, was director of merit; Yin Kaishan, magistrate of Taigu, was headquarters aide; and Sun Shunde, Liu Hongji, Dou Cong, the Yingyang commandant Wang Changxie of Gaoping, Jiang Baoyi of Tianshui, and Yang Tun were appointed left and right army commanders;

sentences.zh: 自餘文武，隨才授任。

translations.literal: the remaining civil and military officials were assigned posts according to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: all other civil and military men were given posts suited to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 又以世子建成為隴西公，左領軍大都督，左三統軍隸焉；

translations.literal: He also made his heir Jiancheng Duke of Longxi, Grand Commander of the Left Army, with the three left army units subordinate to him;
translations.idiomatic: He made his heir Jiancheng Duke of Longxi and Grand Commander of the Left Army, with the three left-wing units under his command;

sentences.zh: 世民為敦煌公，右三統軍隸焉各置官屬。

translations.literal: Shimin was made Duke of Dunhuang, with the three right army units subordinate to him; each was given his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was made Duke of Dunhuang, with the three right-wing units under him; each was given his own staff of officers.

sentences.zh: 以柴紹為右領軍府長史；

translations.literal: Chai Shao was made chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: Chai Shao was appointed chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters;

sentences.zh: 咨議譙人劉贍領西河通守。

translations.literal: the adviser Liu Shan of Qiao was made acting defender of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan of Qiao, a staff adviser, was made acting defender of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 道源名河，開山名嶠，皆以字行。

translations.literal: Daoyuan's given name was He, Kaishan's was Qiao; both were known by their style names.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daoyuan's given name was He and Yin Kaishan's was Qiao; both were known by their style names.

sentences.zh: 開山，不害之孫也。

translations.literal: Kaishan was a grandson of Yin Buhai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kaishan was a grandson of the official Yin Buhai.

sentences.zh: 李密復帥眾向東都，丙申，大戰於平樂園。

translations.literal: Li Mi again led his host toward the Eastern Capital; on the day bingshen, a great battle was fought at Pingle Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi again led his forces toward Luoyang. On the day bingshen they fought a major battle at Pingle Garden.

sentences.zh: 密左騎、右步、中列強弩，鳴千鼓以沖之，東都兵大敗，密復取回洛倉。

translations.literal: Mi placed cavalry on the left, infantry on the right, and powerful crossbows in the center; a thousand drums sounded as they charged; the Eastern Capital troops were utterly defeated, and Mi again seized Huiluo Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi arrayed cavalry on the left, infantry on the right, and powerful crossbows in the center, then charged with a thousand drums beating. The Luoyang army was routed, and Li Mi recaptured Huiluo Granary.

sentences.zh: 突厥遣其柱國康鞘利等送馬千匹詣李淵為互市，許發兵送淵入關，多少隨所欲。

translations.literal: The Turks sent their pillar general Kang Qiaoli and others with a thousand horses to Li Yuan for mutual trade, promising to send troops to escort Yuan into the Pass, as many or as few as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks sent their pillar general Kang Qiaoli and others with a thousand horses for trade with Li Yuan, and promised to send troops to escort him through the Pass—in whatever numbers he desired.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，淵引見康鞘利等，受可汗書，禮容盡恭，贈遣康鞘利等甚厚。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Yuan received Kang Qiaoli and the others in audience, accepted the qaghan's letter, and showed the utmost courtesy and respect, sending Kang Qiaoli and the others away with rich gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, Li Yuan received Kang Qiaoli and his party, accepted the qaghan's letter with full ceremonial courtesy, and sent them away with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 擇其馬之善者，止市其半；

translations.literal: He selected the best of the horses and purchased only half of them;
translations.idiomatic: He chose the best horses and bought only half of them;

sentences.zh: 義士請以私錢市其餘，淵曰：「虜饒馬而貪利，其來將不已，恐汝不能市也。

translations.literal: the Righteous Warriors asked to buy the rest with their private funds; Yuan said: "The barbarians have many horses and are greedy for profit; they will keep coming without end—I fear you cannot afford to buy them all.
translations.idiomatic: the warriors asked to buy the rest with their own money. Li Yuan said: "The Turks have plenty of horses and are greedy for profit. They will keep sending more, and I doubt you could afford to buy them all.

sentences.zh: 吾所以少取者，示貧，且不以為急故也，當為汝貰之，不足為汝費。

translations.literal: The reason I take so few is to show poverty, and also because we do not urgently need them; I shall buy on credit for you—you need not spend your own money."
translations.idiomatic: I am taking so few to appear poor and because we are not desperate for them yet. I will buy the rest on credit for you—you need not spend your own funds."

sentences.zh: 」乙巳，靈壽賊帥郗士陵帥眾數千降於淵，淵以為鎮東將軍、燕郡公，仍置鎮東府，補僚屬，以招撫山東郡縣。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, the bandit chief of Lingshou, Xi Shiling, led several thousand men to surrender to Yuan; Yuan made him General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Yan, and established an Eastern Pacification headquarters, filling out its staff, to win over the commanderies and counties east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, Xi Shiling, a rebel leader from Lingshou, surrendered with several thousand men. Li Yuan made him General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Yan, set up an Eastern Pacification headquarters with a full staff, and charged him with winning over the eastern provinces.

sentences.zh: 己巳，康鞘利北還。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Kang Qiaoli returned north.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi, Kang Qiaoli returned north.

sentences.zh: 淵命劉文靜使於突厥以請兵，私謂文靜曰：「胡騎入中國，生民之大蠹也。

translations.literal: Yuan ordered Liu Wenjing to go on mission to the Turks to request troops, and privately told Wenjing: "When barbarian cavalry enter China, they are a great scourge upon the people.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan sent Liu Wenjing on a mission to the Turks to request troops, and told him privately: "When Turkic cavalry enter China, they are a calamity for the people.

sentences.zh: 吾所以欲得之者，恐劉武周引之共為邊患；

translations.literal: The reason I wish to obtain them is that I fear Liu Wuzhou will draw them in to make trouble together on the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: I want them only because I fear Liu Wuzhou will enlist them to raid our borders;

sentences.zh: 又，胡馬行牧，不費芻粟，聊欲藉之以為聲勢耳。

translations.literal: moreover, barbarian horses graze as they march and cost no fodder or grain—I merely wish to borrow them for their prestige.
translations.idiomatic: and besides, Turkic horses graze as they march and cost us no fodder—I only want to borrow their prestige.

sentences.zh: 數百人之外，無所用之。

translations.literal: Beyond a few hundred men, they are of no use to us."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond a few hundred men, they are useless to us."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，煬帝遣江都通守王世充將江、淮勁卒，將軍王隆帥邛黃蠻，河北大使太常少卿韋霽、河南大使虎牙郎將王辯等各帥所領同赴東都，相知討李密。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Emperor Yang sent the Jiangdu inspector-general Wang Shichong to lead crack troops from the Jiang and Huai regions, the general Wang Long to lead Qiong and Huang barbarians, the Hebei commissioner and Director of Ceremonies Wei Ji, the Henan commissioner and Tiger-Fang commandant Wang Bian, and others, each leading his own forces to converge on the Eastern Capital, to join in attacking Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Emperor Yang dispatched Wang Shichong, inspector-general of Jiangdu, with crack troops from the Jiang-Huai region; General Wang Long with Qiong and Huang tribesmen; Wei Ji, Director of Ceremonies and commissioner for Hebei; Wang Bian, Tiger-Fang commandant and commissioner for Henan; and others—each leading his own forces to Luoyang to coordinate the campaign against Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 霽，世康之子也。

translations.literal: Ji was a son of Wei Shikang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji was a son of Wei Shikang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，李淵以子元吉為太原太守，留守晉陽宮，後事悉委之。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Li Yuan made his son Yuanji Taiyuan governor, to remain and guard the Jinyang palace, entrusting him with all subsequent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renzi, Li Yuan appointed his son Yuanji governor of Taiyuan to guard the Jinyang palace and entrusted him with all affairs there.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，淵帥甲士三萬發晉陽，立軍門誓眾，並移檄郡縣，諭以尊立代王之意；

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Yuan led thirty thousand armored soldiers out from Jinyang, swore an oath before the army gate, and also issued proclamations to the commanderies and counties, explaining the plan to honor and install Prince Dai;
translations.idiomatic: On the day guichou, Li Yuan marched from Jinyang at the head of thirty thousand armored men, took an oath before the army, and issued proclamations to the provinces explaining his plan to enthrone Prince Dai;

sentences.zh: 西突厥阿史那大奈亦帥其眾以從。

translations.literal: Ashina Danai of the Western Turks also led his host to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Danai of the Western Turks also brought his forces to join him.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，遣通議大夫張綸將兵徇稽胡。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, he dispatched the Master of Ceremonies Zhang Lun to lead troops in subduing the Ji Hu.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiayin, he sent Master of Ceremonies Zhang Lun to lead troops against the Ji Hu rebels.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，淵至西河，慰勞吏民，賑贍窮乏；

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Yuan reached Xihe, comforted officials and common people, and provided relief for the destitute;
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Li Yuan reached Xihe, comforted officials and civilians, and distributed relief to the poor;

sentences.zh: 民年七十已上，皆除散官，其餘豪俊，隨才授任，口詢功能，手注官秩，一日除千餘人；

translations.literal: common people aged seventy and above were all granted honorary offices; the remaining eminent men were assigned posts according to talent; he inquired orally into their abilities and wrote in their ranks by hand—more than a thousand were appointed in a single day;
translations.idiomatic: all people aged seventy or above were given honorary offices; other worthy men were appointed according to their abilities—he questioned each orally about his skills and wrote in their ranks by hand, appointing more than a thousand in a single day;

sentences.zh: 受官皆不取告身，各分淵所書官名而去。

translations.literal: those who received office took no formal credentials; each departed with only the office name Yuan had written.
translations.idiomatic: none of them took formal appointment documents—they simply left with the office title Li Yuan had written for each.

sentences.zh: 淵入雀鼠谷；

translations.literal: Yuan entered Queyu Valley;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan entered Queyu Valley;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，軍賈胡堡，去霍邑五十餘里。

translations.literal: on the day renxu, the army camped at Jiahu Fort, more than fifty li from Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: on the day renxu the army encamped at Jiahu Fort, a little over fifty li from Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 代王侑遣虎牙郎將宋老生帥精兵二萬屯霍邑，左武候大將軍屈突通將驍果數萬屯河東以拒淵。

translations.literal: Prince Dai You sent the Tiger-Fang commandant Song Laosheng to lead twenty thousand crack troops to encamp at Huoyi, and the Left Martial Guard general Qutu Tong to lead tens of thousands of elite troops to encamp at Hedong to resist Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dai You sent the Tiger-Fang commandant Song Laosheng with twenty thousand elite troops to hold Huoyi, and the Left Martial Guard general Qutu Tong with tens of thousands of crack troops to hold Hedong against Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 會積雨，淵不得進，遣府佐沈叔安等將羸兵還太原，更運一月糧。

translations.literal: Continuous rain fell; Yuan could not advance and sent his headquarters aides Shen Shu'an and others to lead weak troops back to Taiyuan to transport another month's provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains set in and Li Yuan could not advance. He sent his aide Shen Shu'an and others back to Taiyuan with a weak detachment to fetch another month's supplies.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，張綸克離石，殺太守楊子崇。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Zhang Lun captured Lishi and killed the governor Yang Zichong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, Zhang Lun captured Lishi and killed its governor Yang Zichong.

sentences.zh: 劉文靜至突厥，見始畢可汗，請兵，且與之約曰：「若入長安，民眾土地入唐公，金玉繒帛歸突厥。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing reached the Turks, met Qaghan Shibi, requested troops, and also made this agreement with him: "If we enter Chang'an, the people and land shall go to Duke Tang, while gold, jade, silks, and brocades shall go to the Turks."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing reached the Turkic court, met Qaghan Shibi, and requested troops, agreeing with him: "If we take Chang'an, the people and territory shall belong to Duke Tang, while gold, jade, silks, and brocades shall belong to the Turks."

sentences.zh: 」始畢大喜，丙寅，遣其大臣級失特勒先至淵軍，告以兵已上道。

translations.literal: Shibi was greatly pleased; on the day bingyin, he sent his minister Jishitele ahead to Yuan's army to announce that the troops were already on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi was delighted. On the day bingyin he sent his minister Jishitele ahead to Li Yuan's camp to announce that the troops were already on their way.

sentences.zh: 淵以書招李密。

translations.literal: Yuan sent a letter to recruit Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan sent a letter inviting Li Mi to join him.

sentences.zh: 密自恃兵強，欲為盟主，己巳，使祖君彥復書曰：「與兄派流雖異，根系本同。

translations.literal: Mi, trusting in his strong army, wished to be alliance leader; on the day jisi, he had Zu Junyan reply: "Though our branches differ, our roots are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his military strength, Li Mi wanted to be alliance leader. On the day jisi he had Zu Junyan reply: "Though our branches diverge, our roots are one.

sentences.zh: 自唯虛薄，為四海英雄共推盟主。

translations.literal: I alone am feeble and shallow, yet the heroes of the four seas together have pushed me forward as alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy, yet the heroes of the realm have unanimously made me their leader.

sentences.zh: 所望左提右挈，戮力同心，執子嬰於咸陽，殪商辛於牧野，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: What I hope for is that you will guide me with your left hand and support me with your right, striving together with one heart—to seize Ziying at Xianyang and destroy Shang Xin at Muye; would that not be glorious!
translations.idiomatic: I hope you will guide and support me as we strive together—to seize Ziying at Xianyang and destroy King Zhou at Muye. What glory that would be!

sentences.zh: 」且欲使淵以步騎數千自至河內，面結盟約。

translations.literal: He also wished Yuan to bring several thousand infantry and cavalry in person to Henei to conclude the alliance face to face.
translations.idiomatic: He also wanted Li Yuan to come in person to Henei with several thousand infantry and cavalry to seal the alliance face to face.

sentences.zh: 淵得書，笑曰：「密妄自矜大，非折簡可致。

translations.literal: When Yuan received the letter, he laughed and said: "Mi presumptuously prides himself—he is not someone a brief letter can summon.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan read the letter, he laughed and said: "Li Mi is absurdly arrogant—not someone you can summon with a polite note.

sentences.zh: 吾方有事關中，若遽絕之，乃是更生一敵；

translations.literal: I am now occupied with affairs in Guanzhong; if I abruptly break with him, I would only create another enemy;
translations.idiomatic: I am occupied with Guanzhong right now. If I cut him off abruptly, I would only create another enemy;

sentences.zh: 不如卑辭推獎以驕其志，使為我塞成皋之道，綴東都之兵，我得專意西征。

translations.literal: better to use humble words and praise to inflate his ambition, so that he blocks the Cheng'ao road for me and pins down the Eastern Capital's troops, while I can concentrate on the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: better to flatter him with humble praise, inflate his pride, and let him block the Cheng'ao road and tie down Luoyang's army while I focus on the west.

sentences.zh: 俟關中平定，據險養威，徐觀鷸蚌之勢以收漁人之功，未為晚也。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong is pacified, holding strategic points and nurturing strength, I may slowly watch the snipe-and-clam struggle and reap the fisherman's gain—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guanzhong is secure, I can hold the passes, build my strength, and watch the snipe and clam fight while I reap the fisherman's reward. That will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」乃使溫大雅復書曰：「吾雖庸劣，幸承餘緒，出為八使，入典六屯，顛而不扶，通賢所責。

translations.literal: He then had Wen Daya reply: "Though I am mediocre and inferior, I have fortunately inherited a noble lineage, served abroad as one of the Eight Commissioners, and at home directed the Six Garrisons; to see the dynasty totter and not support it is what any worthy man would condemn.
translations.idiomatic: He had Wen Daya reply: "Though I am unworthy, I have the good fortune of noble lineage. I served abroad as one of the Eight Commissioners and at home directed the Six Garrisons. To see the dynasty tottering and not lend support is what any worthy man would condemn.

sentences.zh: 所以大會義兵，和親北狄，共匡天下，志在尊隋。

translations.literal: Therefore I have gathered righteous troops on a grand scale, allied with the northern barbarians by marriage, and together we set the world aright, with the aim of honoring Sui.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I have raised a great righteous army, allied with the northern tribes, and set out to restore the realm—with the aim of preserving the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 天生烝民，必有司牧。

translations.literal: Heaven gave birth to the multitude; there must be one to tend them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven created the people; there must be one to shepherd them.

sentences.zh: 當今為牧，非子而誰！

translations.literal: Who but you should be that shepherd today!
translations.idiomatic: Who but you should be that shepherd today!

sentences.zh: 老夫年逾知命，願不及此。

translations.literal: This old man has passed the age of fifty and does not aspire to such a role.
translations.idiomatic: I am past fifty and have no such ambition.

sentences.zh: 欣戴大弟，攀鱗附翼，唯弟早膺圖菉，以寧兆民！

translations.literal: I rejoice to support my great younger brother, clinging to the dragon's scales and attaching to its wings—may you soon receive Heaven's mandate and bring peace to the myriad people!
translations.idiomatic: I rejoice to follow my great younger brother, clinging to the dragon's scales and wings—may you soon receive Heaven's mandate and bring peace to the people!

sentences.zh: 宗盟之長，屬籍見容，復封於唐，斯榮足矣。

translations.literal: As head of our clan alliance, if my lineage is accepted and I am enfeoffed again in Tang, that glory is enough for me.
translations.idiomatic: As head of our clan alliance, if my lineage is recognized and I am enfeoffed again as Duke of Tang, that honor is glory enough.

sentences.zh: 殪商辛於牧野，所不忍言；

translations.literal: To destroy Shang Xin at Muye—I cannot bear to speak of it;
translations.idiomatic: As for destroying King Zhou at Muye—I cannot bring myself to speak of it;

sentences.zh: 執子嬰於咸陽，未敢聞命。

translations.literal: to seize Ziying at Xianyang—I dare not accept such a command.
translations.idiomatic: and as for seizing Ziying at Xianyang—I dare not accept such orders.

sentences.zh: 汾晉左右，尚須安輯；

translations.literal: The regions around Fen and Jin still need to be pacified;
translations.idiomatic: The Fen and Jin region still needs pacifying;

sentences.zh: 盟津之會，未暇卜期。

translations.literal: the alliance meeting at Mengjin—I have not yet had leisure to fix a date.
translations.idiomatic: as for a meeting at Mengjin—I have not yet had leisure to set a date.

sentences.zh: 」密得書甚喜。

translations.literal: When Mi received the letter he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was delighted when he received the reply.

sentences.zh: 以示將佐曰：「唐公見推，天下不足定矣！

translations.literal: He showed it to his generals and aides, saying: "Duke Tang has deferred to me—the realm is as good as settled!
translations.idiomatic: He showed it to his officers and said: "Duke Tang has deferred to me—the realm is as good as won!

sentences.zh: 」自是信使往來不絕。

translations.literal: From then on envoys passed back and forth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From then on messengers passed between them without cease.

sentences.zh: 雨久不止，淵軍中糧乏；

translations.literal: The rain would not stop for a long time; Yuan's army ran short of provisions;
translations.idiomatic: The rains would not let up, and Li Yuan's army was running out of food;

sentences.zh: 劉文靜未返，或傳突厥與劉武周乘虛晉陽；

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing had not yet returned, and there were rumors that the Turks and Liu Wuzhou would seize the opportunity to strike Jinyang;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing had not yet returned, and rumors spread that the Turks and Liu Wuzhou would seize the chance to attack Jinyang;

sentences.zh: 淵召將佐謀北還。

translations.literal: Yuan summoned his generals and aides to plan a retreat north.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan called his officers together to plan a retreat north.

sentences.zh: 裴寂等皆曰：「宋老生、屈突通連兵據險，未易猝下。

translations.literal: Pei Ji and the others all said: "Song Laosheng and Qutu Tong have joined forces and hold strategic terrain; they cannot easily be taken in a sudden assault.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji and the others all said: "Song Laosheng and Qutu Tong hold the passes together—they cannot be taken quickly.

sentences.zh: 李密雖雲連和，奸謀難測。

translations.literal: Though Li Mi speaks of alliance, his treacherous designs are hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi talks of alliance, but his schemes are impossible to trust.

sentences.zh: 突厥貪而無信，唯利是視。

translations.literal: The Turks are greedy and faithless, caring only for profit.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are greedy and untrustworthy, caring only for gain.

sentences.zh: 武周，事胡者也。

translations.literal: Wuzhou is one who serves the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou is a client of the Turks.

sentences.zh: 太原一方都會，且義兵家屬在焉，不如還救根本，更圖後舉。

translations.literal: Taiyuan is a great metropolis of the region, and the families of our righteous troops are there; better to return and save our base, and plan another campaign later.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan is a major city, and our soldiers' families are there. We should return to secure our base and plan another campaign later.

sentences.zh: 」李世民曰：「今禾菽被野，何優乏糧！

translations.literal: Li Shimin said: "Now grain and millet cover the fields—why worry about lack of provisions!
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin said: "The fields are full of grain—why worry about supplies!

sentences.zh: 老生輕躁，一戰可擒。

translations.literal: Laosheng is rash and impetuous; one battle will capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng is rash and reckless—we can capture him in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 李密顧戀倉粟，未遑遠略。

translations.literal: Li Mi clings to his granary stores and has no leisure for distant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi is fixated on his granary stores and has no time for grand ambitions.

sentences.zh: 武周與突厥外雖相附，內實相猜。

translations.literal: Though Wuzhou and the Turks are outwardly allied, inwardly they truly suspect each other.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Wuzhou and the Turks are allied in name, they deeply distrust each other.

sentences.zh: 武周雖遠利太原，豈可近忘馬邑！

translations.literal: Though Wuzhou may covet Taiyuan from afar, how could he forget Mayi so close at hand!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wuzhou may covet Taiyuan from afar, but he will not forget Mayi right on his doorstep!

sentences.zh: 本興大義，奮不顧身以救蒼生，當先入咸陽，號令天下。

translations.literal: We originally raised the great cause, throwing ourselves into danger to save the people—we should first enter Xianyang and command the realm.
translations.idiomatic: We raised this righteous cause to save the people at the risk of our lives. We should march first into Xianyang and command the realm.

sentences.zh: 今遇小敵，遽已班師，恐從義之徒一朝解體，還守太原一城之地為賊耳，何以自全！

translations.literal: Now we meet a small enemy and hastily withdraw—I fear those who joined our cause will dissolve in a day; returning to hold only the city of Taiyuan, we would be mere bandits—how could we preserve ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: If we retreat before a minor foe, our followers will scatter overnight. Reduced to defending Taiyuan alone, we would be no better than bandits—how could we survive!

sentences.zh: 」李建成亦以為然。

translations.literal: Li Jiancheng also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiancheng agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 淵不聽，促令引發。

translations.literal: Yuan would not listen and urgently ordered the march to begin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan would not listen and ordered the army to march at once.

sentences.zh: 世民將復入諫，會日暮，淵已寢；

translations.literal: Shimin was about to enter again to remonstrate, but dusk fell and Yuan had already retired;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin was about to go in and remonstrate again, but night had fallen and Li Yuan had already gone to bed;

sentences.zh: 世民不得入，號哭於外，聲聞帳中。

translations.literal: Shimin could not enter and wailed outside; his voice reached inside the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin could not get in and wept aloud outside until his cries reached the tent.

sentences.zh: 淵召問之，世民曰：「今兵以義動，進戰則克，退還則散；

translations.literal: Yuan summoned him and asked; Shimin said: "Now the army moves on righteousness—advance to battle and we conquer, retreat and we scatter;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan summoned him and asked what was wrong. Shimin said: "This army fights for a righteous cause—advance and we win, retreat and we dissolve;

sentences.zh: 眾散於前，敵乘於後，死亡無日，何得不悲！

translations.literal: the host scatters before us, the enemy presses from behind—death is imminent; how could I not weep!
translations.idiomatic: our men scatter before us while the enemy closes in from behind—death is certain. How could I not weep!

sentences.zh: 」淵乃悟，曰：「軍已發，奈何？

translations.literal: Yuan then understood and said: "The army has already marched—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan understood and said: "The army has already marched—what can we do?

sentences.zh: 」世民曰：「右軍嚴而未發；

translations.literal: Shimin said: "The right wing is drawn up but has not yet departed;
translations.idiomatic: Shimin said: "The right wing is drawn up but has not yet departed;

sentences.zh: 左軍雖去，計亦未遠，請自追之。

translations.literal: though the left wing has gone, they cannot have gone far—I ask leave to pursue them myself."
translations.idiomatic: the left wing has left but cannot be far yet. Let me go after them myself."

sentences.zh: 」淵笑曰：「吾之成敗皆在爾，知復何言，唯爾所為。

translations.literal: Yuan smiled and said: "My success or failure rests entirely with you—what more is there to say? Do as you will."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan smiled and said: "My success or failure rests entirely with you. Say no more—do as you see fit."

sentences.zh: 」世民乃與建成分道夜追左軍復還。

translations.literal: Shimin then split with Jiancheng by separate routes and pursued the left wing through the night, bringing them back.
translations.idiomatic: Shimin and Jiancheng then split up and pursued the left wing through the night, bringing them back.

sentences.zh: 丙子，太原運糧亦至。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the grain transport from Taiyuan also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi, the grain convoy from Taiyuan also arrived.

sentences.zh: 武威鷹揚府司馬李軌，家富，好任俠。

translations.literal: Li Gui, marshal of the Yingyang headquarters in Wuwei, came from a wealthy family and loved chivalrous adventure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui, marshal of the Yingyang headquarters in Wuwei, came from a wealthy family with a taste for bold adventure.

sentences.zh: 薛舉作亂於金城，軌與同郡曹珍、關謹、梁碩、李贇、安修仁等謀曰：「薛舉必來侵暴，郡官庸怯，勢不能御，吾輩豈可束手並妻孥為人所虜邪！

translations.literal: When Xue Ju rebelled at Jincheng, Gui plotted with his fellow townsman Cao Zhen, Guan Jin, Liang Shuo, Li Yun, An Xiuren, and others, saying: "Xue Ju will surely come to invade and ravage; the commandery officials are mediocre and cowardly and cannot resist—how can we sit with folded hands and let our wives and children be captured!
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Ju rebelled at Jincheng, Li Gui plotted with his fellow townsman Cao Zhen, Guan Jin, Liang Shuo, Li Yun, An Xiuren, and others: "Xue Ju will surely come to plunder us. The commandery officials are timid and useless—they cannot defend us. How can we sit idle while our families are taken captive!

sentences.zh: 不若相與並力拒之，保據河右以待天下之變。

translations.literal: Better to join our strength together to resist him, hold the lands west of the Yellow River, and await the changes of the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Let us join forces to resist him, hold the lands west of the Yellow River, and wait for the realm to change."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆以為然，欲推一人為主，各相讓，莫肯當。

translations.literal: All agreed and wished to push one man forward as leader; each deferred to the others, and none would accept.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed and wanted to choose a leader, but each deferred to the others and none would accept.

sentences.zh: 曹珍曰：「久聞圖讖李氏當王；

translations.literal: Cao Zhen said: "I have long heard that prophetic texts say the house of Li is destined to rule;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhen said: "I have long heard prophetic texts say the house of Li is destined to rule;

sentences.zh: 今軌在謀中，乃天命也。

translations.literal: now Gui appears in these prophecies—this is Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui appears in those prophecies—this is Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 」遂相與拜軌，奉以為主。

translations.literal: They then together bowed to Gui and made him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: They bowed to Li Gui together and made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，軌令修仁集諸胡，軌結民間豪傑，共起兵，執虎賁郎將謝統師、郡丞韋士政。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Gui ordered Xiuren to gather the various barbarians; Gui rallied local heroes, and together they raised troops, seizing the Tiger-Fang commandant Xie Tongshi and the assistant magistrate Wei Shizheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Li Gui ordered An Xiuren to gather the tribal peoples while he rallied local heroes. Together they rose in arms and seized the Tiger-Fang commandant Xie Tongshi and the assistant magistrate Wei Shizheng.

sentences.zh: 軌自稱河西大涼王，置官屬並擬開皇故事。

translations.literal: Gui styled himself Great King of Liang west of the River, established officials, and modeled his institutions on those of the Kaihuang era.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui declared himself Great King of Liang west of the River, appointed officials, and modeled his government on the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 關謹等欲盡殺隋官，分其家貲，軌曰：「諸人既逼以為主，當稟其號令。

translations.literal: Guan Jin and the others wished to kill all the Sui officials and divide their household wealth; Gui said: "Since you forced me to be your leader, you should obey my commands.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Jin and the others wanted to kill all the Sui officials and divide their property. Li Gui said: "You forced me to be your leader—you should obey my commands.

sentences.zh: 今興義兵以救生民，乃殺人取貨，此群盜耳，將何以濟！

translations.literal: Now we raise righteous troops to save the people—yet you would kill for goods; that is mere banditry; how will that succeed!
translations.idiomatic: We are raising a righteous army to save the people, yet you would kill for loot—that is mere banditry. How will that succeed!

sentences.zh: 」於是以統師為太僕卿，士政為太府卿。

translations.literal: He then made Tongshi Director of the Imperial Stud and Shizheng Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Xie Tongshi Director of the Imperial Stud and Wei Shizheng Director of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 西突厥闕達度設據會寧川，自稱闕可汗，請降於軌。

translations.literal: Que Datushe of the Western Turks held Huining Valley, styled himself Qaghan Que, and asked to surrender to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Que Datushe of the Western Turks held Huining Valley, declared himself Qaghan Que, and offered to submit to Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 薛舉自稱秦帝，立其妻鞠氏為皇后，子仁果為皇太子。

translations.literal: Xue Ju styled himself Emperor of Qin, made his wife Lady Ju empress, and his son Renguo crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju declared himself Emperor of Qin, made his wife Lady Ju empress, and his son Renguo crown prince.

sentences.zh: 遣仁果將兵圍天水，克之，舉自金城徙都之。

translations.literal: He sent Renguo to lead troops and besiege Tianshui; when it was taken, Ju moved his capital there from Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Renguo to besiege Tianshui. When it fell, Xue Ju moved his capital there from Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 仁果多力，善騎射，軍中號萬人敵；

translations.literal: Renguo was very strong and skilled at mounted archery; in the army he was called a match for ten thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Renguo was immensely strong and skilled at mounted archery—the army called him a match for ten thousand men;

sentences.zh: 然性貪而好殺。

translations.literal: yet his nature was greedy and he loved killing.
translations.idiomatic: but he was greedy and bloodthirsty by nature.

sentences.zh: 嘗獲庾信子立，怒其不降，磔於火上，稍割以啖軍士。

translations.literal: Once he captured Yu Xin's son Li, angry that he would not surrender; he dismembered him on a fire and gradually cut off pieces to feed the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Once he captured Yu Xin's son Li, who refused to surrender. Enraged, he dismembered him over a fire and fed pieces to his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 及克天水，悉召富人，倒懸之，以醋灌鼻，責其金寶。

translations.literal: When he captured Tianshui, he summoned all the wealthy, hung them upside down, poured vinegar into their nostrils, and demanded their gold and jewels.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Tianshui, he summoned the wealthy, hung them upside down, poured vinegar into their nostrils, and extorted their gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 舉每戒之曰：「汝之才略足以辦事，然苛虐無恩，終當覆我國家。

translations.literal: Ju often warned him: "Your talent and resourcefulness are sufficient for affairs, yet you are harsh and cruel without mercy—you will ultimately overturn our state."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju often warned him: "Your talent is sufficient for any task, but your cruelty and lack of mercy will ultimately destroy our state."

sentences.zh: 舉遣晉王仁越將兵趨劍口，至河池郡；

translations.literal: Ju sent Prince of Jin Renguo to lead troops toward Jiankou, reaching Hechi commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju sent Prince of Jin Renguo toward Jiankou, reaching Hechi Commandery;

sentences.zh: 太守蕭瑀拒卻之。

translations.literal: the governor Xiao Yu repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: where Governor Xiao Yu repelled him.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將常仲興濟河擊李軌，與軌將李贇戰於昌松，仲興舉軍敗沒。

translations.literal: He also sent his general Chang Zhongxing to cross the river and attack Li Gui; at Changsong he fought Gui's general Li Yun, and Zhongxing's entire army was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his general Chang Zhongxing across the river to attack Li Gui. At Changsong he fought Li Gui's general Li Yun, and Chang Zhongxing's entire army was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 軌欲縱遣之，斌曰：「力戰獲俘，復縱以資敵，將焉用之！

translations.literal: Gui wished to release them; Yun said: "We fought hard to take prisoners, then release them to strengthen the enemy—of what use is that!
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui wanted to release them. Li Yun said: "We fought hard to capture them—why release them to strengthen the enemy!

sentences.zh: 不如盡坑之。

translations.literal: Better to bury them all alive."
translations.idiomatic: Better to bury them all alive."

sentences.zh: 」軌曰：「天若祚我，當擒其主，此屬終為我有；

translations.literal: Gui said: "If Heaven blesses me, I shall capture their leader, and these men will ultimately be mine;
translations.idiomatic: Li Gui said: "If Heaven favors me, I will capture their leader and these men will ultimately be mine;

sentences.zh: 若其無成，留此何益！

translations.literal: if we achieve nothing, what good is keeping them!
translations.idiomatic: if we fail, what good are they to us!

sentences.zh: 」乃縱之。

translations.literal: He then released them.
translations.idiomatic: He released them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，攻張掖、敦煌、西平、□包罕，皆克之，盡有河西五郡之地。

translations.literal: Before long he attacked Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping, and [Paohan], taking them all, and possessed the five commanderies west of the River in their entirety.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he attacked Zhangye, Dunhuang, Xiping, and Paohan, capturing them all and holding the five commanderies west of the River.

sentences.zh: 煬帝詔左御衛大將軍涿郡留守薛世雄將燕地精兵三萬討李密，命王世充等諸將皆受世雄節度，軍所過盜賊隨便誅剪。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang ordered the Left Imperial Guard general and Zhuo commandery garrison commander Xue Shixiong to lead thirty thousand crack troops from the Yan region against Li Mi, commanding Wang Shichong and the other generals under his authority; wherever the army passed, bandits were executed as encountered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered Xue Shixiong, general of the Left Imperial Guard and garrison commander of Zhuo, to lead thirty thousand crack troops from the Yan region against Li Mi, with Wang Shichong and the other generals under his command. Wherever the army passed, bandits were killed on sight.

sentences.zh: 世雄行至河間，軍於七里井，竇建德士眾惶懼，悉拔諸城南遁，聲言還入豆子。

translations.literal: When Shixiong reached Hejian, he encamped at Qili Well; Dou Jiande's soldiers and people were fearful and pulled out of all the cities southward, claiming they would return to Douzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shixiong reached Hejian, he encamped at Qili Well. Dou Jiande's men were terrified and abandoned all the southern cities, claiming they would retreat to Douzi.

sentences.zh: 世雄以為畏己，不復設備，建德謀還襲之。

translations.literal: Shixiong thought they feared him and took no further precautions; Jiande planned to turn back and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong thought they feared him and let his guard down. Jiande planned a counterattack.

sentences.zh: 其處去世雄營百四十里，建德帥敢死士二百八十人先行，令餘眾續發，建德與其士眾約曰：「夜至，則擊其營；

translations.literal: His position was one hundred forty li from Shixiong's camp; Jiande led two hundred eighty dare-to-die men ahead, ordering the rest to follow; Jiande made this agreement with his troops: "If we arrive by night, we strike their camp;
translations.idiomatic: His camp was one hundred forty li from Shixiong's. Jiande led two hundred eighty dare-to-die men ahead, with the rest to follow. He told his men: "If we arrive by night, we attack their camp;

sentences.zh: 已明，則降之。

translations.literal: if day has broken, we surrender."
translations.idiomatic: if day has broken, we surrender."

sentences.zh: 」未至一里所，天欲明，建德惶惑議降；

translations.literal: Before they had gone one li, dawn was near; Jiande was anxious and confused and discussed surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Before they had gone one li, dawn was approaching. Jiande grew anxious and talked of surrender;

sentences.zh: 會天大霧，人咫尺不相辨，建德喜曰：「天讚我也！

translations.literal: then a great fog fell, and men could not distinguish each other even at arm's length; Jiande rejoiced: "Heaven approves of me!
translations.idiomatic: then a thick fog descended so that men could not see each other at arm's length. Jiande exclaimed: "Heaven favors me!

sentences.zh: 」遂突入其營擊之，世雄士卒大亂，皆騰柵走。

translations.literal: He then burst into their camp and attacked; Shixiong's soldiers fell into great disorder and all leaped the palisades and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed their camp. Shixiong's men panicked and fled over the palisades.

sentences.zh: 世雄不能禁，與左右數十騎遁歸涿郡，慚恚發病卒。

translations.literal: Shixiong could not restrain them; with several dozen horsemen of his entourage he fled back to Zhuo commandery, where shame and rage brought on illness and death.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong could not stop them. He fled to Zhuo with a few dozen horsemen, where shame and rage brought on an illness that killed him.

sentences.zh: 建德遂圍河間。

translations.literal: Jiande then besieged Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande then besieged Hejian.

sentences.zh: 八月，己卯，雨霽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jimao, the rain cleared.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jimao, the rain finally stopped.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，李淵命軍中曝鎧仗行裝。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Li Yuan ordered the army to air out armor, weapons, and baggage.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, Li Yuan ordered the army to air out its armor, weapons, and baggage.

sentences.zh: 辛巳旦，東南由山足細道趣霍邑。

translations.literal: At dawn on the day xinsi, they advanced southeast along a narrow path at the foot of the mountains toward Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the day xinsi, they advanced southeast along a narrow mountain path toward Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 淵恐宋老生不出，李建成、李世民曰：「老生勇而無謀，以輕騎挑之，理無不出；

translations.literal: Yuan feared Song Laosheng would not come out; Li Jiancheng and Li Shimin said: "Laosheng is brave but lacks strategy; provoke him with light cavalry and by reason he cannot fail to come out;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan feared Song Laosheng would not come out. Li Jiancheng and Li Shimin said: "Laosheng is brave but stupid. Provoke him with light cavalry and he is bound to come out;

sentences.zh: 脫其固守，則誣以貳於我。

translations.literal: if he stubbornly holds his position, slander him as having gone over to our side.
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses to budge, accuse him of secretly siding with us.

sentences.zh: 彼恐為左右所奏，安敢不出！

translations.literal: He will fear being reported by those around him—how would he dare not come out!"
translations.idiomatic: He will fear being denounced by his own men—he will have to come out!"

sentences.zh: 」淵曰：「汝測之善，老生不能逆戰賈胡，吾知其無能為也！

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Your judgment is sound; Laosheng could not face battle at Jiahu—I know he is incapable of anything!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said: "Your judgment is sound. Laosheng would not fight at Jiahu—I know he is good for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 」淵與數百騎先至霍邑城東數里以待步兵，使建成、世民將數十騎至城下，舉鞭指麾，若將圍城之狀，且詬之。

translations.literal: Yuan with several hundred horsemen went first to several li east of Huoyi city to await the infantry, sending Jiancheng and Shimin with several dozen horsemen to the foot of the city wall, raising their whips and gesturing as if about to besiege the city, and reviling them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan rode ahead with several hundred horsemen to a point several li east of Huoyi to await the infantry, while Jiancheng and Shimin took several dozen horsemen to the city wall, gesturing with their whips as if preparing to besiege it and hurling insults.

sentences.zh: 老生怒，引兵三萬自東門、南門分道而出，淵使殷開山趣召後軍。

translations.literal: Laosheng was enraged and led thirty thousand men out by separate routes from the east and south gates; Yuan sent Yin Kaishan hurrying to summon the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng flew into a rage and led thirty thousand men out through the east and south gates. Li Yuan sent Yin Kaishan to hurry up the rear army.

sentences.zh: 後軍至，淵欲使軍士先食而戰，世民曰：「時不可失。

translations.literal: When the rear army arrived, Yuan wished to let the soldiers eat first and then fight; Shimin said: "The moment must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: When the rear army arrived, Li Yuan wanted the men to eat before fighting. Shimin said: "We cannot lose this moment."

sentences.zh: 」淵乃與建成陳於城東，世民陳於城南。

translations.literal: Yuan then arrayed with Jiancheng east of the city, and Shimin south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan arrayed with Jiancheng east of the city and Shimin south of it.

sentences.zh: 淵、建成戰小卻，世民與軍頭臨淄段志玄自南原引兵馳下，沖老生陳，出其背，世民手殺數十人，兩刀皆缺，流血滿袖，灑之復戰。

translations.literal: Yuan and Jiancheng's battle gave ground slightly; Shimin with the army leader Duan Zhixuan of Linzi led troops charging down from the southern heights, broke Laosheng's formation, and came out behind him; Shimin personally killed several dozen men; both his blades were notched; blood soaked his sleeves; he shook it off and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan and Jiancheng's line gave ground slightly. Shimin and the army leader Duan Zhixuan of Linzi charged down from the southern heights, broke through Laosheng's formation, and struck from behind. Shimin personally killed dozens of men. Both his blades were notched and blood soaked his sleeves, but he shook it off and fought on.

sentences.zh: 淵兵復振，因傳呼曰：「已獲老生矣！

translations.literal: Yuan's troops rallied again, and a cry was passed along: "We have already captured Laosheng!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan's troops rallied, and a cry went through the ranks: "We have captured Laosheng!

sentences.zh: 」老生兵大敗，淵兵先趣其門，門閉，老生下馬投塹，劉弘基就斬之，殭屍數里。

translations.literal: Laosheng's troops were utterly defeated; Yuan's troops rushed first for the gate; the gate was closed; Laosheng dismounted and threw himself into the moat; Liu Hongji went up and beheaded him; corpses lay for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng's army was routed. Li Yuan's men raced for the gate, but it was shut. Laosheng dismounted and threw himself into the moat. Liu Hongji went down and beheaded him. Corpses lay for miles.

sentences.zh: 日已暮，淵即命登城，時無攻具，將士肉薄而登，遂克之。

translations.literal: The sun had already set; Yuan immediately ordered the city stormed; there were no siege engines; officers and soldiers climbed by pressing close with their flesh and took it.
translations.idiomatic: By evening Li Yuan ordered the city taken. With no siege engines, the soldiers scaled the walls by sheer force of numbers and captured it.

sentences.zh: 淵賞霍邑之功，軍吏疑奴應募者不得與良人同，淵曰：「矢石之間，不辨貴賤；

translations.literal: Yuan rewarded the merit of Huoyi; army officers doubted whether slave recruits should share equally with free men; Yuan said: "Amid arrows and stones, noble and base are not distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan rewarded the victors of Huoyi. Some officers questioned whether slave recruits should share equally with free men. Li Yuan said: "In the hail of arrows, noble and base are not distinguished;

sentences.zh: 論勳之際，何有等差，宜並從本勳授。

translations.literal: when discussing merit, what place has rank? All should receive rewards according to their actual merit."
translations.idiomatic: when discussing merit, what place has rank? All should be rewarded according to their actual deeds."

sentences.zh: 」壬午，淵引見霍邑吏民，勞賞如西河，選其丁壯使從軍；

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Yuan received in audience the officials and common people of Huoyi, comforted and rewarded them as at Xihe, and selected able-bodied men to join the army;
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu, Li Yuan received the officials and people of Huoyi, comforted and rewarded them as he had at Xihe, and drafted able-bodied men into the army;

sentences.zh: 關中軍士欲歸者，並授五品散宮，遣歸。

translations.literal: soldiers from Guanzhong who wished to return home were all granted fifth-rank honorary palace offices and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: soldiers from Guanzhong who wished to go home were all given fifth-rank honorary offices and sent back.

sentences.zh: 或諫以官太濫，淵曰：「隋氏吝惜勳賞，此所以失人心也，奈何效之！

translations.literal: Some remonstrated that offices were given too freely; Yuan said: "The house of Sui was stingy with rewards for merit—that is why it lost the people's hearts; why should we imitate that!
translations.idiomatic: Some objected that he was giving away offices too freely. Li Yuan said: "The Sui dynasty was stingy with rewards—that is why it lost the people's hearts. Why should we imitate that!

sentences.zh: 且收眾以官，不勝於用兵乎！

translations.literal: Besides, winning the multitude with offices—is that not better than using troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, winning people over with offices—is that not better than fighting them!"

sentences.zh: 丙戌，淵入臨汾郡，慰撫如霍邑。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Yuan entered Linfen commandery and comforted the people as at Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu, Li Yuan entered Linfen Commandery and comforted the people as he had at Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，宿鼓山。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, he lodged at Drum Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengyin, he camped at Drum Mountain.

sentences.zh: 絳郡通守陳叔達拒守；

translations.literal: Chen Shuda, inspector-general of Jiang commandery, held out and resisted;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda, inspector-general of Jiang Commandery, held out against him;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，進攻，克之。

translations.literal: on the day xinmao, they advanced to attack and took it.
translations.idiomatic: on the day xinmao they attacked and captured it.

sentences.zh: 叔達，陳高宗之子，有才學，淵禮而用之。

translations.literal: Shuda was a son of Emperor Gao of Chen, talented and learned; Yuan treated him with courtesy and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda was a son of Emperor Gao of Chen, a man of talent and learning whom Li Yuan treated with courtesy and employed.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，淵至龍門，劉文靜、康鞘利以突厥兵五百人、馬二千匹來至。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Yuan reached Longmen; Liu Wenjing and Kang Qiaoli arrived with five hundred Turkic soldiers and two thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: On the day guisi, Li Yuan reached Longmen. Liu Wenjing and Kang Qiaoli arrived with five hundred Turkic soldiers and two thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 淵喜其來緩，謂文靜曰：「吾西行及河，突厥始至，兵少馬多，皆君將命之功也。

translations.literal: Yuan was pleased they had come slowly and said to Wenjing: "I marched west and reached the river before the Turks arrived—few soldiers but many horses; this is all the merit of your carrying out my orders."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan was pleased they had arrived late and told Wenjing: "I reached the river before the Turks came—few soldiers but many horses. This is entirely thanks to your carrying out my orders."

sentences.zh: 汾陽薛大鼎說淵：「請勿攻河東，自龍門直濟河，據永豐倉，傳檄遠近，關中可坐取也。

translations.literal: Xue Dading of Fenyang advised Yuan: "Please do not attack Hedong; cross the river directly from Longmen, seize Yongfeng Granary, issue proclamations near and far—Guanzhong can be taken while sitting."
translations.idiomatic: Xue Dading of Fenyang advised Li Yuan: "Do not attack Hedong. Cross the river directly from Longmen, seize Yongfeng Granary, and issue proclamations far and wide—Guanzhong can be taken without a fight."

sentences.zh: 」淵將從之。

translations.literal: Yuan was about to follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan was about to follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 諸將請先攻河東，乃以大鼎為大將軍府察非掾。

translations.literal: The generals asked to attack Hedong first, so he made Dading an investigator of misconduct in the Grand General's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The generals insisted on attacking Hedong first, so he made Xue Dading an investigator in the Grand General's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 河東縣戶曹任瑰說淵曰：「關中豪傑皆企踵以待義兵。

translations.literal: Ren Gui, revenue clerk of Hedong county, said to Yuan: "The heroes of Guanzhong all stand on tiptoe awaiting the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui, revenue clerk of Hedong county, told Li Yuan: "The heroes of Guanzhong are all waiting eagerly for the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 瑰在馮翊積年，知其豪傑，請往諭之，必從風而靡。

translations.literal: I have been in Fengyi for many years and know its heroes; I ask to go and persuade them—they will surely follow the wind and bend."
translations.idiomatic: I have lived in Fengyi for years and know its leaders. Let me go persuade them—they will surely flock to your banner."

sentences.zh: 義師自梁山濟河，指韓城，逼郃陽。

translations.literal: The righteous army, from Mount Liang crossing the river, aimed at Hancheng and pressed on Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: The righteous army crossed the river from Mount Liang, marched on Hancheng, and pressed toward Heyang.

sentences.zh: 蕭造文吏，必望塵請服。

translations.literal: Xiao Zao is a civil official—he will surely beg submission at sight of dust.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zao is only a civil official; he is sure to surrender at the first glimpse of your dust.

sentences.zh: 孫華之徒，皆當遠迎，然後鼓行而進，直據永豐。

translations.literal: Sun Hua and his kind should all welcome from afar, then beat drums and advance, seizing Yongfeng directly.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Sun Hua should all come out to welcome you from afar; then you can march forward with drums beating and seize Yongfeng outright.

sentences.zh: 雖未得長安，關中固已定矣。

translations.literal: Though Chang'an is not yet taken, Guanzhong is surely already settled.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you have not yet taken Chang'an, Guanzhong will already be as good as secured.

sentences.zh: 」淵說，以瑰為銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Yuan was pleased and appointed Gui as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan was persuaded and appointed Ren Gui Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 時關中群盜，孫華最強。

translations.literal: At that time among the bandit hosts of Guanzhong, Sun Hua was strongest.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, among the rebel bands in Guanzhong, Sun Hua was the most powerful.

sentences.zh: 丙申，淵至汾陰，以書招之。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Yuan reached Fenyin and summoned him by letter.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, Li Yuan reached Fenyin and wrote to summon him.

sentences.zh: 己亥，淵進軍壺口，河濱之民獻舟者日以百數，乃置水軍。

translations.literal: On jihai, Yuan advanced to Hukou; people on the riverside presenting boats numbered in the hundreds each day, so he established a naval force.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Li Yuan advanced to Hukou. River folk brought boats by the hundreds each day, and he accordingly formed a navy.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，孫華自郃陽輕騎渡河見淵。

translations.literal: On renyin, Sun Hua from Heyang with light cavalry crossed the river to see Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Sun Hua rode light cavalry from Heyang across the river to meet Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 淵握手與坐，慰獎之，以華為左光祿大夫、武鄉縣公，領馮翊太守，其徒有功者，委華以次授官，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Yuan took his hand and seated him, comforted and rewarded him, made Hua Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Wuxiang, acting as Grand Defender of Fengyi; those among his followers with merit—entrusted to Hua to grant offices in order—rewards very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan took his hand, seated him beside him, and comforted and praised him. He appointed Sun Hua Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Wuxiang, with acting authority as Grand Defender of Fengyi. Merit among his followers was entrusted to Sun Hua for sequential appointment to office, and the rewards were lavish.

sentences.zh: 使之先濟；

translations.literal: He had them cross first;
translations.idiomatic: He had them cross the river first.

sentences.zh: 繼遣左右統軍王長諧、劉弘基及左領軍長史陳演壽、金紫光祿大夫史大柰將步騎六千自梁山濟，營於河西以待大軍。

translations.literal: Then sent Left and Right Unified Army commanders Wang Changxie, Liu Hongji, and Left Army Inspector Registrar Chen Yanshou, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal Shi Dana with six thousand foot and horse from Mount Liang to cross, encamped on the west of the river to await the great army.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Wang Changxie and Liu Hongji, the Left and Right Unified Army commanders, together with Chen Yanshou, registrar of the Left Army Inspectorate, and Shi Dana, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal, leading six thousand infantry and cavalry across from Mount Liang to camp on the west bank and await the main force.

sentences.zh: 以任瑰為招慰大使，瑰說韓城，下之。

translations.literal: He made Ren Gui Pacification Commissioner; Gui persuaded Hancheng, and it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Ren Gui pacification commissioner. Ren Gui persuaded Hancheng to surrender.

sentences.zh: 淵謂長諧等曰：「屈突通精兵不少，相去五十餘里，不敢來戰，足明其眾不為之用。

translations.literal: Yuan said to Changxie and others: "Qutu Tong has no few elite troops; some fifty-odd li apart, he dares not come fight—enough to show his masses do not serve him willingly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan told Wang Changxie and the others: "Qutu Tong commands a considerable elite force. Though only fifty-odd li away, he dares not give battle—proof enough that his men are not willing to fight for him.

sentences.zh: 然通畏罪，不敢不出。

translations.literal: Yet Tong fears punishment and dares not not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Still, Tong fears punishment and will be forced to move sooner or later.

sentences.zh: 若自濟河擊卿等，則我進攻河東，必不能守；

translations.literal: If he himself crosses the river to attack you gentlemen, then I will advance and attack Hedong—he surely cannot hold it;
translations.idiomatic: If he crosses the river himself to strike you, I shall advance on Hedong and he will surely be unable to hold it.

sentences.zh: 若全軍守城，則卿等絕其河梁：前扼其喉，後拊其背，彼不走必為擒矣。

translations.literal: If his whole army holds the city, then you gentlemen cut his river bridge: choke his throat in front, strike his back from behind—if he does not flee, he will surely be captured."
translations.idiomatic: If he keeps his entire army in the city, you can sever his river crossing: choke him in front and strike his rear. If he does not flee, he is sure to be taken."

sentences.zh: 」驍果從煬帝在江都者多逃去，帝患之，以問裴矩，對曰：「人情非有匹偶，難以久處，請聽軍士於此納室。

translations.literal: Many of the Xiaoguo following Emperor Yang at Jiangdu had fled; the emperor was troubled and asked Pei Ju, who replied: "Human feeling has no fixed partner—hard to stay long together; please allow the soldiers here to take wives."
translations.idiomatic: Many of the elite troops who had followed Emperor Yang to Jiangdu had deserted. The emperor was troubled and asked Pei Ju, who answered: "Men cannot live without companions for long. Please allow the soldiers to take wives here."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，悉召江都境內寡婦、處女集宮下，恣將士所取；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he summoned all widows and maidens within Jiangdu territory to gather below the palace and let the officers and soldiers take as they pleased;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he summoned all widows and unmarried women in the Jiangdu region to assemble below the palace, where officers and soldiers were free to choose among them.

sentences.zh: 或先與奸者聽自首，即以配之。

translations.literal: Some who had previously committed adultery were allowed to confess, then matched to them.
translations.idiomatic: Women who had previously had illicit relations were permitted to confess and were then assigned to the men in question.

sentences.zh: 武陽郡丞元寶藏以郡降李密，甲寅，密以寶藏為上柱國、武陽公。

translations.literal: Wuyang Assistant Prefect Yuan Baocang submitted the commandery to Li Mi; on jiayin, Mi made Baocang Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang, assistant prefect of Wuyang, surrendered the commandery to Li Mi. On jiayin, Mi appointed Baocang Supreme Pillar of State and Duke of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 寶藏使其客巨鹿魏徵為啟謝密，且請改武陽為魏州；

translations.literal: Baocang had his retainer Julu Wei Zheng write a letter thanking Mi, and also asked to change Wuyang to Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Baocang had his client Wei Zheng of Julu compose a letter of thanks to Li Mi and also requested that Wuyang be renamed Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 又請帥所部西取魏郡，南會諸將取黎陽倉。

translations.literal: He also asked to lead his troops west to take Weijun, south to join the generals in taking the Liyang granary.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked to lead his forces west to seize Wei Commandery and south to join the other generals in capturing the Liyang granary.

sentences.zh: 密喜，即以寶藏為魏州總管，召魏徵為元帥府文學參軍，掌記室。

translations.literal: Mi was pleased and immediately made Baocang Military Commissioner of Weizhou, summoned Wei Zheng as Literary Staff Officer of the Marshal's Headquarters, in charge of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was delighted. He at once appointed Baocang military commissioner of Weizhou and summoned Wei Zheng to serve as literary staff officer at marshal headquarters, in charge of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 征少孤貧，好讀書，有大志，落拓不事生業。

translations.literal: Zheng from youth was orphaned and poor, loved reading, had great ambition, was unruly and did not pursue a livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng had been orphaned and poor from childhood. He loved books and cherished lofty ambitions, but lived freely and would not settle into any regular trade.

sentences.zh: 始為道士，寶藏召典書記。

translations.literal: He had first been a Taoist priest; Baocang summoned him to manage clerical records.
translations.idiomatic: He had first become a Taoist priest before Baocang summoned him to keep his written records.

sentences.zh: 密愛其文辭，故召之。

translations.literal: Mi loved his literary style, hence summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi admired his writing, and so brought him into his service.

sentences.zh: 初，貴鄉長弘農魏德深，為政清靜，不嚴而治。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief of Guixiang Hongnong Wei Deshen governed with quiet purity, ruling without severity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Deshen of Hongnong, chief magistrate of Guixiang, had governed with quiet clarity and achieved order without harshness.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，徵稅百端，使者旁午，責成郡縣，民不堪命，唯貴鄉閭裡不擾，有無相通，不竭其力，所求皆給。

translations.literal: During the Liaodong campaign, levies were manifold, envoys came and went unceasingly, pressing county and commandery to deliver—people could not bear their lives; only Guixiang hamlets were undisturbed, the haves and have-nots aiding each other, not exhausting their strength, every demand met.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign, taxes and levies multiplied in every form. Envoys shuttled back and forth, pressing counties and commanderies to deliver. The people could hardly survive, yet in Guixiang the neighborhoods remained undisturbed. Neighbors shared what they had, did not exhaust themselves, and met every demand.

sentences.zh: 元寶藏受詔捕賊，數調器械，動以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Yuan Baocang received orders to capture bandits, repeatedly requisitioned equipment, constantly applying military law.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang had been ordered to hunt down bandits. He repeatedly requisitioned equipment and routinely enforced military law.

sentences.zh: 其鄰城營造，皆聚於聽事，官吏遞相督責，晝夜喧囂，猶不能濟。

translations.literal: In neighboring cities' construction, all gathered in the audience hall, officials taking turns supervising and blaming, day and night clamorous, still unable to finish.
translations.idiomatic: In neighboring cities all construction work was crowded into the government hall. Officials took turns supervising and rebuking one another day and night in ceaseless uproar, yet still could not finish on time.

sentences.zh: 德深聽隨便修營，官府寂然，恆若無事，唯戒吏以不須過勝餘縣，使百姓勞苦；

translations.literal: Deshen allowed repairs wherever convenient; the government offices were silent, always as if nothing were happening, only admonishing clerks not to exceed other counties and make the people toil;
translations.idiomatic: Deshen let people carry out repairs wherever convenient. The government offices stayed quiet and always seemed as if nothing were afoot. He only warned his clerks not to outdo neighboring counties and wear the people down.

sentences.zh: 然民各自竭心，常為諸縣之最，縣民愛之如父母。

translations.literal: Yet the people each exhausted their hearts; he was constantly first among the counties; the county people loved him as parents.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the people gave their utmost willingly. His district was constantly foremost among the counties, and the people loved him as they would their parents.

sentences.zh: 寶藏深害其能，遣將千兵赴東都。

translations.literal: Baocang deeply resented his ability and sent a general with a thousand troops to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Baocang deeply resented his competence and sent a general with a thousand men to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 所領兵聞寶藏降密，思其親戚，輒出都門，東向慟哭而返；

translations.literal: The troops he led, hearing Baocang had submitted to Mi, thought of their kin, promptly left the capital gate, faced east weeping bitterly and returned;
translations.idiomatic: When the troops under his command heard that Baocang had surrendered to Li Mi, they thought of their families, left the city gate at once, turned eastward, wept bitterly, and marched back.

sentences.zh: 或勸之降密，皆泣曰：「我與魏明府同來，何忍棄去！

translations.literal: Some urged them to surrender to Mi; all wept and said: "We came together with Magistrate Wei—how can we bear to abandon him!"
translations.idiomatic: Some urged them to surrender to Li Mi. They all wept and said: "We came here with Magistrate Wei. How can we bear to desert him!"

sentences.zh: 河南、山東大水，餓殍滿野，煬帝詔開黎陽倉賑之，吏不時給，死者日數萬人。

translations.literal: Henan and Shandong suffered great floods; corpses of the starved filled the fields. Emperor Yang ordered the Liyang granary opened for relief, but officials did not distribute in time, and the dead numbered tens of thousands each day.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and Shandong were ravaged by flood. The starving lay dead across the countryside. Emperor Yang ordered the Liyang granary opened for relief, but officials failed to distribute grain promptly, and tens of thousands died each day.

sentences.zh: 徐世勣言於李密曰：「天下大亂，本為饑饉。

translations.literal: Xu Shiji said to Li Mi: "The empire is in great disorder, fundamentally because of famine.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji said to Li Mi: "The empire is in chaos above all because of famine.

sentences.zh: 今更得黎陽倉，大事濟矣。

translations.literal: Now further obtaining the Liyang granary, the great affair is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we have the Liyang granary as well, the great enterprise can succeed.

sentences.zh: 」密遣世績帥麾下五千人自原武濟河，會元寶藏、郝孝德、李文相及洹水賊帥張升、清河賊帥趙君德共襲破黎陽倉，據之，開倉恣民就食，浹旬間，得勝兵二十餘萬。

translations.literal: Mi sent Xu Shiji leading five thousand under his command from Yuanwu to cross the river, joining Yuan Baocang, Hao Xiaode, Li Wenxiang, and the bandit chiefs of Huan River Zhang Sheng and of Qinghe Zhao Junde to together storm and break the Liyang granary, seize it, open the granary and let the people eat freely; within ten days, obtained more than two hundred thousand battle-ready troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi sent Xu Shiji at the head of five thousand men under his command to cross the river from Yuanwu. Together with Yuan Baocang, Hao Xiaode, Li Wenxiang, Zhang Sheng the Huan River bandit chief, and Zhao Junde the Qinghe bandit chief, they jointly stormed and captured the Liyang granary. They held it, opened the stores, and let the people eat freely. Within ten days they had more than two hundred thousand battle-ready troops.

sentences.zh: 武安、永安、義陽、弋陽、齊郡相繼降密。

translations.literal: Wu'an, Yong'an, Yiyang, Yiyang, and Qi commanderies submitted to Mi in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wu'an, Yong'an, Yiyang of Yi, Yiyang of Yi Prefecture, and Qi Commandery surrendered to Li Mi one after another.

sentences.zh: 竇建德、朱粲之徒亦遣使附密，密以粲為揚州總管、鄧公。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande, Zhu Can, and their kind also sent envoys to attach themselves to Mi; Mi made Can Military Commissioner of Yangzhou and Duke of Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande, Zhu Can, and others also sent envoys to join Li Mi. Mi appointed Zhu Can military commissioner of Yangzhou and Duke of Deng.

sentences.zh: 泰山道士徐洪客獻書於密，以為：「大眾久聚，恐米盡人散，師老厭戰，難可成功。

translations.literal: Mount Tai Taoist priest Xu Hongke presented a letter to Mi, holding that: "The masses have long gathered—fearing grain exhausted and men scattered, the army weary and loathing battle—success is hard.
