translations.idiomatic: The Mount Tai Taoist Xu Hongke submitted a letter to Li Mi arguing that the great host had been gathered too long: grain might run out and men scatter, the army would grow weary and lose the will to fight, and success would be hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 」勸密「乘進取之機，因士馬之銳，沿流東指，直向江都，執取獨夫，號令天下。

translations.literal: He urged Mi: "Seize the moment of advance, rely on the sharpness of warriors and horses, follow the current eastward, straight to Jiangdu, seize the lone man, and command the empire."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Li Mi to seize the moment for advance, exploit the sharpness of his troops and horses, sail downriver toward Jiangdu, seize the tyrant, and command the empire.

sentences.zh: 」密壯其言，以書招之，洪客竟不出，莫知所之。

translations.literal: Mi admired his words, summoned him by letter; Hongke ultimately did not appear, and no one knew where he went.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was impressed by his counsel and wrote to summon him, but Hongke never came forth and his whereabouts were unknown.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，張綸徇龍泉、文成等郡，皆下之，獲文成太守鄭元□。

translations.literal: On yimao, Zhang Lun subdued Longquan, Wencheng, and other commanderies, all submitting; he captured Wencheng Grand Defender Zheng Yuan[n].
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Zhang Lun marched against Longquan, Wencheng, and other commanderies, all of which submitted. He captured Zheng Yuan[n], grand defender of Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 元□，譯之子也。

translations.literal: Yuan[n] was the son of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuan[n] was the son of Zheng Yi.

sentences.zh: 屈突通遣虎牙郎將桑顯和將驍果數千人夜襲王長諧等營，長諧等戰不利，孫華、史大柰以游騎自後擊顯和，大破之。

translations.literal: Qutu Tong sent Tiger Tooth General Sang Xianhe with several thousand Xiaoguo to night-assault the camp of Wang Changxie and others; Changxie and the rest fought poorly; Sun Hua and Shi Dana with mobile cavalry struck Xianhe from the rear and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Qutu Tong sent the Tiger Tooth general Sang Xianhe with several thousand elite troops to raid Wang Changxie's camp by night. Wang Changxie and his men fared badly until Sun Hua and Shi Dana hit Xianhe from the rear with light cavalry and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 顯和脫走入城，仍自絕河梁。

translations.literal: Xianhe escaped and fled into the city, then himself severed the river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Xianhe broke free and fled into the city, then destroyed the river crossing himself.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，馮翊大守蕭造降於李淵。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Fengyi Grand Defender Xiao Zao surrendered to Li Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Xiao Zao, grand defender of Fengyi, surrendered to Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 造，修之子也。

translations.literal: Zao was the son of Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zao was the son of Xiao Xiu.

sentences.zh: 戊午，淵帥諸軍圍河東，屈突通嬰城自守。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Yuan led the armies to besiege Hedong; Qutu Tong clung to the city and held himself in defense.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Li Yuan led his forces to besiege Hedong, while Qutu Tong shut himself in the city and defended it stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 將佐復推淵領太尉，增置官屬，淵從之。

translations.literal: The aides again urged Yuan to take the post of Grand Marshal and added official posts; Yuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: His staff again urged Li Yuan to assume the post of grand marshal and expand his staff of officials, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 時河東未下，三輔豪傑至者日以千數。

translations.literal: At that time Hedong was not yet taken; heroes of the Three Assistants arriving numbered more than a thousand each day.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong had not yet fallen, but heroes from the Three Assistants region were arriving by the thousand each day.

sentences.zh: 淵欲引兵西趣長安，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Yuan wished to lead troops west toward Chang'an but hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan wanted to march west toward Chang'an but still hesitated and could not decide.

sentences.zh: 裴寂曰：「屈突通擁大眾，憑堅城，吾捨之而去，若進攻長安不克，退為河東所踵，腹背受敵，此危道也。

translations.literal: Pei Ji said: "Qutu Tong holds a great host and relies on a strong city. If we abandon him and leave, and if attacking Chang'an does not succeed, we retreat and are trampled by Hedong—enemy front and rear—we receive attack on belly and back; this is a perilous path.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji said: "Qutu Tong commands a large force behind strong walls. If we leave him and march away, and if we fail to take Chang'an, we will be caught from behind by Hedong. We would be attacked from front and rear. That is a dangerous course.

sentences.zh: 不若先克河東，然後西上。

translations.literal: Better first to overcome Hedong, then go west.
translations.idiomatic: It is better to take Hedong first and then march west.

sentences.zh: 長安恃通為援，通敗，長安必破矣。

translations.literal: Chang'an relies on Tong as its support; when Tong is defeated, Chang'an is sure to fall.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an depends on Tong for support. Once he is beaten, Chang'an is sure to fall.

sentences.zh: 」李世民曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Li Shimin said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin said: "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 兵貴神速，吾席累勝之威，撫歸附之眾，鼓行而西，長安之人望風震駭，智不及謀，勇不及斷，取之若振槁葉耳。

translations.literal: Soldiers prize swiftness. Relying on our accumulated victories, reassuring the submitted masses, beating drums and marching west—the people of Chang'an will tremble at the wind; wisdom cannot reach to counsel, courage cannot reach to decide—taking it is like shaking down dead leaves.
translations.idiomatic: Speed is the soul of war. With the prestige of our repeated victories and the morale of those who have joined us, we need only march west with drums beating. The people of Chang'an will be struck with terror. They will lack the wit to plan and the nerve to act. Taking the city will be like shaking leaves from a withered branch.

sentences.zh: 若淹留自弊於堅城之下，彼得成謀修備以待我，坐費日月，眾心離沮，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: If we linger and wear ourselves out below a strong city, they gain time to form plans and repair defenses to await us, sitting and wasting days and months, the masses' hearts scattered and discouraged—then the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If we waste ourselves besieging a stronghold, they will have time to devise plans and strengthen their defenses. Days and months will slip away, morale will collapse, and the great enterprise will be lost.

sentences.zh: 且關中蜂起之將，未有所屬，不可不早招懷也。

translations.literal: Moreover the rising leaders of Guanzhong have as yet no allegiance—they cannot be recruited too late.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the rebel leaders rising in Guanzhong have not yet chosen a master. We cannot wait too long to win them over.

sentences.zh: 屈突通自守虜耳，不足為慮。

translations.literal: Qutu Tong is a self-defending captive—he is not worth worrying over.
translations.idiomatic: Qutu Tong is only a man shut up in his own fortress. He is not worth worrying about."

sentences.zh: 」淵兩從之，留諸將圍河東，自引軍而西。

translations.literal: Yuan followed both sides, left the generals to besiege Hedong, and himself led the army west.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan took advice from both sides: he left his generals to besiege Hedong and marched west himself.

sentences.zh: 朝邑法曹武功靳孝謨，以蒲津、中水單二城降，華陰令李孝常以永豐倉降，仍應接河西諸軍。

translations.literal: Chaoyi Law Clerk Wugong Jin Xiaomo surrendered the two cities of Pujin and Zhongshui alone; Huayin Magistrate Li Xiaochang surrendered the Yongfeng granary and still linked up with the armies west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xiaomo, law clerk of Chaoyi in Wugong, surrendered the two cities of Pujin and Zhongshui by himself. Li Xiaochang, magistrate of Huayin, surrendered the Yongfeng granary and continued to coordinate with the armies west of the river.

sentences.zh: 孝常，圓通之子也。

translations.literal: Xiaochang was the son of Yuantong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaochang was the son of Li Yuantong.

sentences.zh: 京兆諸縣亦多遣使請降。

translations.literal: The counties of Jingzhao also mostly sent envoys requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the counties in the Jingzhao region likewise sent envoys offering to surrender.

sentences.zh: 王世充、韋霽、王辯及河內通守孟善誼、河陽郡尉獨孤武都各帥所領會東都，唯王隆後期不至。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, Wei Ji, Wang Bian, and Hedong Communications Commissioner Meng Shanyi and Heyang Commandery Captain Dugu Wudu each led their forces to assemble at the Eastern Capital; only Wang Long arrived late and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, Wei Ji, Wang Bian, Meng Shanyi the communications commissioner of the interior, and Dugu Wudu the commandery captain of Heyang each led their troops to gather at the Eastern Capital. Only Wang Long was late and failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 己未，越王侗使虎賁郎將劉長恭等帥留守兵，寵玉等帥偃師兵，與世充等合十餘萬眾，擊李密於洛口，與密夾洛水相守。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent Tiger Guard General Liu Changgong and others to lead the garrison troops, and Chongyu and others to lead the Yanshi troops, joining Shichong and the rest in more than a hundred thousand men to strike Li Mi at Luokou, facing Mi across the Luo River in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Yang Tong, Prince of Yue, sent Liu Changgong, a Tiger Guard general, and others to command the garrison troops, and Chongyu and others to lead the Yanshi troops. Together with Wang Shichong and the rest they mustered more than a hundred thousand men and attacked Li Mi at Luokou, facing him across the Luo in a standoff.

sentences.zh: 煬帝詔諸軍皆受世充節度。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang decreed that all armies were subject to Shichong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered that all the armies were to obey Wang Shichong's command.

sentences.zh: 帝遣攝江都郡丞馮慈明向東都，為密所獲，密素聞其名，延坐勞問，禮意甚厚，因謂曰：「隋祚已盡，公能與孤共立大功乎？

translations.literal: The emperor sent Acting Jiangdu Assistant Prefect Feng Ciming toward the Eastern Capital; he was captured by Mi. Mi had long heard his name, extended a seat and questioned him with labor, courtesy very thick, and therefore said to him: "The house of Sui is exhausted—can you together with me establish great merit?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Feng Ciming, acting assistant prefect of Jiangdu, toward the Eastern Capital, but Li Mi captured him. Mi had long known his reputation. He seated him, questioned him warmly, and treated him with great courtesy. Then he said: "The Sui dynasty is finished. Will you join me in accomplishing great deeds?"

sentences.zh: 」慈明曰：「公家歷事先朝，榮祿兼備。

translations.literal: Ciming said: "Your family served the former dynasty through generations, glory and salary both complete.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ciming replied: "Your clan served the former dynasty for generations and enjoyed both honor and emolument.

sentences.zh: 不能善守門閥，乃與玄感舉兵，偶脫罔羅，得有今日，唯圖反噬，未諭高旨。

translations.literal: Unable to guard your gate and clan well, you then raised troops with Xuan Gan; by chance escaping the net, you have today—only plotting rebellion, not yet understanding the high intent.
translations.idiomatic: You could not keep your house in order, yet you rose with Yang Xuan'gan. By luck you escaped the net and have come to this day, only to turn against your sovereign. You do not yet grasp the higher purpose.

sentences.zh: 莽、卓、敦、玄非不強盛，一朝夷滅，罪及祖宗。

translations.literal: Wang Mang, Zhuo, Dun, and Xuan were not without strength, yet in one morning they were extinguished, and guilt reached their ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang, Dong Zhuo, Wang Dun, and Murong Xuan were none of them weak, yet each was destroyed in a day, and ruin reached their forebears.

sentences.zh: 僕死而後已，不敢聞命！

translations.literal: Your servant dies and then stops—dare not hear the command!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall serve to the death and dare not obey your order!"

sentences.zh: 」密怒，囚之。

translations.literal: Mi was angry and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi was enraged and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 慈明說防人席務本，使亡走。

translations.literal: Ciming persuaded the guard Xi Wuben to let him flee.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ciming persuaded his guard Xi Wuben to help him escape.

sentences.zh: 奉表江都，及致書東都論賊形勢，至雍丘，為密將李公逸所獲，密又義而釋之；

translations.literal: He presented a memorial to Jiangdu and also sent letters to the Eastern Capital discussing the rebels' situation; reaching Yongqiu, he was captured by Mi's general Li Gongyi; Mi again released him out of righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: He sent a memorial to Jiangdu and letters to the Eastern Capital describing the rebels' situation. At Yongqiu he was seized by Li Mi's general Li Gongyi, but Mi again released him out of respect for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 出至營門，翟讓殺之。

translations.literal: When he went out to the camp gate, Zhai Rang killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the camp gate, Zhai Rang killed him.

sentences.zh: 慈明，子琮之子也。

translations.literal: Ciming was the son of Zicong.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ciming was the son of Feng Zicong.

sentences.zh: 密之克洛口也，箕山府郎將張季珣固守不下，密以其寡弱，遣人呼之。

translations.literal: When Mi captured Luokou, Jishan Garrison Colonel Zhang Jixiong held fast and would not submit; Mi, seeing his few and weak, sent men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi took Luokou, Zhang Jixiong, colonel of the Jishan garrison, held firm and refused to submit. Seeing how few and weak he was, Mi sent men to call on him.

sentences.zh: 季珣罵密極口，密怒，遣兵攻之，不能克。

translations.literal: Jixiong cursed Mi to the utmost; Mi was angry and sent troops to attack but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jixiong cursed Li Mi roundly. Enraged, Mi sent troops to attack him but could not take the place.

sentences.zh: 時密眾數十萬在其城下，季珣四面阻絕，所領不過數百人，而執志彌固，誓以必死。

translations.literal: At that time Mi's masses numbered hundreds of thousands below his city; Jixiong was cut off on all four sides, those he led not exceeding several hundred men, yet his resolve was firmer, vowing certain death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Mi had hundreds of thousands of men below the city, while Zhang Jixiong was cut off on every side with no more than a few hundred followers. Yet his resolve only hardened, and he swore to die rather than yield.

sentences.zh: 久之，糧盡水竭，士卒羸病，季珣撫循之，一無離叛，自三月至於是月，城遂陷。

translations.literal: After long time, grain exhausted and water spent, soldiers emaciated and ill; Jixiong comforted and guided them, not one deserting; from the third month until this month, the city finally fell.
translations.idiomatic: In time grain and water ran out and his soldiers grew weak and sick. Zhang Jixiong cared for them, and not one deserted. From the third month until this month the city finally fell.

sentences.zh: 季珣見密不肯拜，曰：「天子爪牙，何容拜賊！

translations.literal: Jixiong saw Mi and would not bow, saying: "The Son of Heaven's talon and fang—how can one bow to a bandit!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jixiong saw Li Mi he refused to bow, saying: "I am the Son of Heaven's claw and fang. How can I bow to a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 」密猶欲降之，誘諭終不屬，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Mi still wished to win him over, enticed and instructed him, but in the end he would not submit, so he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi still wished to win him over and tried persuasion, but Zhang Jixiong would not submit in the end, so Mi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 季珣，祥子之子也。

translations.literal: Jixiong was the son of Xiangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jixiong was the son of Zhang Xiangzi.

sentences.zh: 庚申，李淵帥諸軍濟河；

translations.literal: On gengshen, Li Yuan led the armies to cross the river;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Li Yuan led his forces across the river.

sentences.zh: 甲子，至朝邑，捨於長春宮，關中士民歸之者如市。

translations.literal: On jiazi, he reached Chaoyi, lodged at Everlasting Spring Palace; scholars and commoners of Guanzhong submitting were like a market.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he reached Chaoyi and lodged at Everlasting Spring Palace. Scholars and commoners of Guanzhong flocked to him like shoppers at a market.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，淵遣世子建成、司馬劉文靜帥王長諧等諸軍數萬人屯永豐倉，守潼關以備東方兵，慰撫使竇軌等受其節度；

translations.literal: On bingyin, Yuan sent the heir apparent Jiancheng and Marshal Liu Wenjing leading Wang Changxie and other armies numbering tens of thousands to encamp at the Yongfeng granary, guard Tong Pass to prepare against eastern troops, with Pacification Commissioners Dou Gui and others under their command;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Li Yuan sent the heir apparent Li Jiancheng and Marshal Liu Wenjing at the head of Wang Changxie and other commanders with tens of thousands of men to encamp at the Yongfeng granary, guard Tong Pass against troops from the east, and place Pacification Commissioner Dou Gui and others under their command.

sentences.zh: 敦煌公世民帥劉弘基等諸軍數萬人徇渭北，慰撫使殷開山等受其節度。

translations.literal: Prince of Dunhuang Shimin led Liu Hongji and other armies numbering tens of thousands to subdue the north bank of the Wei, with Pacification Commissioner Yin Kaishan and others under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dunhuang, Li Shimin, led Liu Hongji and others with tens of thousands of men to sweep the north bank of the Wei, with Pacification Commissioner Yin Kaishan and others under his command.

sentences.zh: 軌，琮之兄也。

translations.literal: Gui was the elder brother of Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Gui was the elder brother of Dou Cong.

sentences.zh: 冠氏長於志寧、安養尉顏師古及世民婦兄弟長孫無忌謁見淵於長春宮。

translations.literal: Chief of Guanshi Yu Zhiming, Anyang Captain Yan Shigu, and Li Shimin's brothers-in-law Zhangsun Wuji paid their respects to Yuan at Everlasting Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhiming, chief of Guanshi, Yan Shigu, captain of Anyang, and Zhangsun Wuji, Li Shimin's brother-in-law, came to pay their respects to Li Yuan at Everlasting Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 師古名籀，以字行。

translations.literal: Shigu's name was Zhou; he went by his style.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shigu's personal name was Zhou; he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 志寧，宣敏之兄子；

translations.literal: Zhiming was the nephew of Xuanmin's elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhiming was the nephew of Yu Xuanmin's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 師古，之推之孫也；

translations.literal: Shigu was the grandson of Zhitui;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shigu was the grandson of Yan Zhitui.

sentences.zh: 皆以文學知名，無忌仍有才略。

translations.literal: All were renowned for literary learning; Wuji moreover had talent and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: All were famed for literary accomplishment, and Wuji also possessed talent and strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 淵皆禮而用之，以志寧為記室，師古為朝散大夫，無忌為渭北行軍典簽。

translations.literal: Yuan all treated them with ceremony and employed them, making Zhiming Recorder, Shigu Court Gentleman for Scattered Service, and Wuji Staff Officer for the Wei North Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan honored them all and put them to use: he made Yu Zhiming recorder, Yan Shigu court gentleman for scattered service, and Zhangsun Wuji staff officer for the Wei north campaign.

sentences.zh: 屈突通聞淵西入，署鷹揚郎將湯陽堯君素領河東通守，使守蒲板，自引兵數萬趣長安，為劉文靜所遏。

translations.literal: When Qu Tutong heard that Yuan had marched west, he appointed the Eagle-Feathered General Yao Junsu of Tangyang as acting Hedong communications commissioner, had him hold Puban, and himself led tens of thousands of troops toward Chang'an, but was blocked by Liu Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Li Yuan had advanced west, Qu Tutong named Yao Junsu of Tangyang—an Eagle-Feathered general—to act as Hedong communications commissioner and hold Puban, while he himself took tens of thousands of men toward Chang'an; Liu Wenjing intercepted him.

sentences.zh: 將軍劉綱戍潼關，屯都尉南城，通欲往依之，王長諧先引兵襲斬綱，據城以拒通，通退保北城。

translations.literal: The general Liu Gang garrisoned Tong Pass and was stationed at Dudu South City; Tutong wished to go rely on him, but Wang Changhe first led troops in a surprise attack and beheaded Gang, seized the city to resist Tutong, and Tutong fell back to defend North City.
translations.idiomatic: General Liu Gang held Tong Pass from Dudu South City. Tutong meant to join him, but Wang Changhe struck first, killed Gang, and held the city against Tutong, who withdrew to the north citadel.

sentences.zh: 淵遣其將呂紹宗等攻河東，不能克。

translations.literal: Yuan sent his generals Lü Shaozong and others to attack Hedong but could not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan sent Lü Shaozong and other generals against Hedong, but they could not take it.

sentences.zh: 柴紹之自長安赴太原也，謂其妻李氏曰：「尊公舉兵，今偕行則不可，留此則及禍，奈何？

translations.literal: When Chai Shao was leaving Chang'an for Taiyuan, he said to his wife Lady Li: "Your honored father has raised troops; I cannot go with you now, yet if I stay here I will meet disaster—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: As Chai Shao set out from Chang'an for Taiyuan, he told his wife Lady Li: "Your father has risen in arms. I cannot take you with me, yet if I leave you here you will come to harm—what shall we do?

sentences.zh: 」李氏曰：「君弟速行，我一婦人，易以潛匿，當自為計。

translations.literal: " Lady Li said: "You, my younger brother-in-law, hurry on your way; I am only a woman and can easily hide myself—I will make my own plans.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li replied: "Go quickly, brother-in-law. I am only a woman and can hide easily; I will see to myself.

sentences.zh: 」紹遂行。

translations.literal: " Shao then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Shao went on his way.

sentences.zh: 李氏歸鄠縣別墅，散家貲，聚徒眾。

translations.literal: Lady Li returned to the villa estate in Hu County, distributed the family wealth, and gathered a band of followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li withdrew to the family villa in Hu County, spent out the household goods, and rallied a following.

sentences.zh: 淵從弟神通在長安，亡入鄠縣山中，與長安大俠史萬寶等起兵以應淵。

translations.literal: Yuan's cousin Shentong was in Chang'an; he fled into the mountains of Hu County and, with the great knight of Chang'an Shi Wanbao and others, raised troops in response to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan's cousin Li Shentong was in Chang'an; he fled into the Hu County hills and, with Chang'an's champion Shi Wanbao and others, raised forces in Li Yuan's support.

sentences.zh: 西域商胡何潘仁入司竹園為盜，有眾數萬，劫前尚書右衛李綱為長史，李氏使其奴馬三寶說潘會與之就神通，合勢攻鄠縣，下之。

translations.literal: He Panren, a merchant from the Western Regions, entered Sizhu Garden as a bandit with a following of tens of thousands; he seized the former Minister of the Right Guard Li Gang to serve as chief clerk. Lady Li had her slave Ma Sanbao persuade Pan Hui to join Shentong; combining their forces they attacked Hu County and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The Sogdian merchant He Panren had turned bandit in Sizhu Garden with a following of tens of thousands and forced the former Minister of the Right Guard Li Gang to serve as his chief clerk. Lady Li sent her servant Ma Sanbao to win He Panren over to Li Shentong; together they stormed Hu County and took it.

sentences.zh: 神通眾逾一萬，自稱關中道行軍總管，以前東城長令狐德棻為記室。

translations.literal: Shentong's forces exceeded ten thousand; he styled himself Commander-in-Chief of the Guanzhong Campaign, and appointed the former chief of Dongcheng Linghu Defen as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shentong's force passed ten thousand. He styled himself Commander-in-Chief of the Guanzhong Campaign and made the former chief of Dongcheng, Linghu Defen, his recorder.

sentences.zh: 德棻，熙之子也。

translations.literal: Defen was the son of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Defen was a son of Linghu Xi.

sentences.zh: 李氏又使馬三寶說群盜李仲文、向善志、丘師利等，皆帥眾從之。

translations.literal: Lady Li again had Ma Sanbao persuade the bandit chiefs Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, Qiu Shili, and others; all led their followers to join her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li again sent Ma Sanbao to win over the bandit leaders Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, Qiu Shili, and others, and each brought his men to her side.

sentences.zh: 仲文，密之從父；

translations.literal: Zhongwen was Mi's paternal uncle;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongwen was a paternal uncle of Li Mi;

sentences.zh: 師利，和之子也。

translations.literal: Shili was He's son.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shili was a son of He.

sentences.zh: 西京留守屢遣兵討潘仁等，皆為所敗。

translations.literal: The Western Capital garrison repeatedly sent troops to attack He Panren and the others, but was defeated each time.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Capital garrison sent troops against He Panren and his allies again and again, and was beaten every time.

sentences.zh: 李氏徇盩厔、武功、始平，皆下之，眾至七萬。

translations.literal: Lady Li marched on Zhouzhi, Wugong, and Shiping—all fell—and her force grew to seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li overran Zhouzhi, Wugong, and Shiping, took them all, and swelled to seventy thousand men.

sentences.zh: 左親衛段綸，文振之子也，娶淵女，亦聚徒於藍田，得萬餘人。

translations.literal: Duan Lun of the Left Personal Guard, son of Wen Zhen, had married Yuan's daughter; he also gathered followers at Lantian and mustered more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Lun of the Left Personal Guard—son of Yuwen Wen Zhen and husband to Li Yuan's daughter—also raised a band at Lantian and gathered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 及淵濟河，神通、李氏、綸各遣使迎淵。

translations.literal: When Yuan crossed the river, Shentong, Lady Li, and Lun each sent envoys to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan crossed the Yellow River, Li Shentong, Lady Li, and Duan Lun each sent envoys to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 淵以神通為光祿大夫，子道彥為朝請大夫，綸為金紫光祿大夫；

translations.literal: Yuan appointed Shentong as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, his son Daoyan as Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, and Lun as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan made Li Shentong a Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, his son Daoyan a Gentleman for Imperial Audiences, and Duan Lun a Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon;

sentences.zh: 使柴紹將數百騎並南山迎李氏。

translations.literal: he sent Chai Shao with several hundred horsemen along the southern mountains to welcome Lady Li.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Chai Shao with several hundred horsemen along the southern hills to fetch Lady Li.

sentences.zh: 何潘仁、李仲文、向善志及關中群盜，皆請降於淵，淵一一以書慰勞授官，使各居其所，受敦煌公世民節度。

translations.literal: He Panren, Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, and the bandits of Guanzhong all asked to surrender to Yuan; Yuan comforted and rewarded each with letters and appointments, letting them remain in their places under the command of the Prince of Dunhuang, Shimin.
translations.idiomatic: He Panren, Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, and the Guanzhong bandits all offered submission to Li Yuan. He answered each with letters of comfort and an office, left them in their districts, and placed them under the Prince of Dunhuang, Li Shimin.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書領京兆內史衛文開年老，聞淵兵向長安，憂懼成疾，不復預事，獨左翊衛將軍陰世師、京兆郡丞骨儀奉代王侑乘城拒守。

translations.literal: Wei Wenkai, Minister of Justice and concurrent Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was old; hearing Yuan's army was marching on Chang'an, worry and fear brought on illness and he no longer attended to affairs. Only the Left Wing Guard general Yin Shishi and the Jingzhao assistant magistrate Gu Yi, on behalf of Prince of Dai You, manned the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wenkai, Minister of Justice and concurrent Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, was elderly. When he heard Li Yuan's army was bearing on Chang'an, anxiety and fear laid him low and he ceased to govern. Only the Left Wing Guard general Yin Shishi and the Jingzhao assistant magistrate Gu Yi, for the Prince of Dai Yang You, held the walls in defense.

sentences.zh: 己巳，淵如蒲津；

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Yuan went to Pujin;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jisi, Li Yuan went to Pujin;

sentences.zh: 庚午，自臨晉濟渭，至永豐倉勞軍，開倉賑饑民。

translations.literal: on the day gengwu he crossed the Wei from Linjin, reached Yongfeng Granary to review the troops, and opened the granaries to relieve the famine-stricken people.
translations.idiomatic: on the day gengwu he crossed the Wei from Linjin, came to Yongfeng Granary to review the army, and opened the stores to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 辛未，還長春宮；

translations.literal: On the day xinwei he returned to Changchun Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinwei he returned to Changchun Palace;

sentences.zh: 壬申，進屯馮翊。

translations.literal: on the day renshen he advanced and encamped at Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: on the day renshen he moved forward and encamped at Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 世民所至，吏民及群盜歸之如流。

translations.literal: Wherever Shimin went, officials and commoners and bandits flocked to him like a current.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Li Shimin went, officials, commoners, and bandits streamed to him.

sentences.zh: 世民收其豪俊以備僚屬，營於涇陽，勝兵九萬。

translations.literal: Shimin enrolled their outstanding men to fill his staff, encamped at Jingyang, and had ninety thousand effectives.
translations.idiomatic: He took their best men into his staff, made camp at Jingyang, and mustered ninety thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 李氏將精兵萬餘會世民於渭北，與柴紹各置幕府，號「娘子軍」。

translations.literal: Lady Li led more than ten thousand picked troops to join Shimin north of the Wei; she and Chai Shao each set up a headquarters, called the "Lady's Army."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li brought more than ten thousand elite troops to meet Li Shimin north of the Wei. She and Chai Shao each raised a separate headquarters, styled the "Lady's Army."

sentences.zh: 先是，平涼奴賊數萬圍扶風太守竇璡，數月不下，賊軍食盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, tens of thousands of "servant bandits" from Pingliang had besieged the prefect of Fufeng, Dou Jin, for months without taking the city; the rebel army's food was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, tens of thousands of Pingliang "servant bandits" had besieged the Fufeng prefect Dou Jin for months without success, until the rebels' provisions ran out.

sentences.zh: 丘師利遣其弟行恭帥五百人負米麥持牛酒詣奴賊營，奴帥長揖，行恭手斬之，謂其眾曰：「汝輩皆良人，何故事奴為主，使天下謂之奴賊！

translations.literal: Qiu Shili sent his younger brother Xinggong to lead five hundred men bearing rice, wheat, cattle, and wine to the servant-bandit camp; the slave chief bowed with hands clasped, and Xinggong cut him down with his own hand, saying to the crowd: "You are all good people—why do you serve slaves as masters and let the world call you 'servant bandits'!
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shili sent his younger brother Xinggong with five hundred men carrying grain, cattle, and wine to the servant-bandit camp. The slave chief bowed with clasped hands; Xinggong struck him down with his own hand and told the crowd: "You are all decent folk—why serve slaves as masters and let the world name you 'servant bandits'!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆俯伏曰：「願改事公。

translations.literal: " The crowd all prostrated themselves and said: "We wish to serve you instead, my lord.
translations.idiomatic: They all prostrated themselves and said: "We wish to serve you, lord.

sentences.zh: 」行恭即帥其眾與師得共謁世民於渭北，世民以為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " Xinggong at once led his followers together with Shide to call on Shimin north of the Wei; Shimin appointed him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Xinggong at once led his men, together with Shide, to present themselves to Li Shimin north of the Wei, and Li Shimin made him a Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 璡，琮之從子也。

translations.literal: Jin was a nephew of Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin was a nephew of Dou Cong.

sentences.zh: 隰城尉房玄齡謁世民於軍門，世民一見如舊識，署記室參軍，引為謀主。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling, district captain of Suicheng, called on Shimin at the army gate; Shimin at first sight treated him like an old acquaintance, appointed him Registrar on the staff, and took him as his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, district captain of Suicheng, presented himself at Li Shimin's gate. Li Shimin received him as though they had long known each other, named him Registrar on the staff, and made him his chief planner.

sentences.zh: 玄齡亦自以遇知己，罄竭心力，知無不為。

translations.literal: Xuanling also felt he had met a true confidant and poured out his mind and strength, leaving nothing undone that he knew how to do.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling, for his part, believed he had found a true patron and gave his mind and strength without reserve, doing all he knew to do.

sentences.zh: 淵命劉弘基、殷開山分兵西略扶風，有眾六萬，南渡渭水，屯長安故城。

translations.literal: Yuan ordered Liu Hongji and Yin Kaishan to divide their forces and march west to reduce Fufeng; they had sixty thousand men, crossed the Wei southward, and encamped at the old city of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan ordered Liu Hongji and Yin Kaishan to divide forces and strike west into Fufeng. They had sixty thousand men, crossed the Wei to the south, and encamped at the old Chang'an city.

sentences.zh: 城中出戰，弘基逆擊，破之。

translations.literal: The city sent troops out to fight; Hongji met them and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: The city sortied; Hongji met them head-on and broke them.

sentences.zh: 世民引兵趣司竹，李仲文、何潘仁、向善志皆帥眾從之，頓於阿城，勝兵十三萬，軍令嚴整，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Shimin led his army toward Sizhu; Li Zhongwen, He Panren, and Xiang Shanzhi all led their followers in his train; he halted at Echeng with one hundred thirty thousand effectives; military discipline was strict—not even a hair was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin marched on Sizhu. Li Zhongwen, He Panren, and Xiang Shanzhi all followed with their bands. He halted at Echeng with one hundred thirty thousand effectives; discipline was iron—nothing was taken, not even a blade of grass.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，世民自盩厔遣使白淵，請期日赴長安。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Shimin from Zhouzhi sent a messenger to inform Yuan and request a date to advance on Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yihai, Li Shimin sent word from Zhouzhi to Li Yuan, asking for a day to march on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 淵曰：「屈突東行不能復西，不足虞矣！

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Qu [Tutong], having gone east, cannot return west—he is not worth worrying about!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan said: "Qu Tutong has gone east and cannot turn back west—he is nothing to fear!

sentences.zh: 」乃命建成選倉上精兵自新豐趣長樂宮，世民帥新附諸軍北屯長安故城，至並聽教。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Jiancheng to select the best troops from the granaries and hurry from Xinfeng toward Changle Palace; Shimin was to command the newly attached armies and encamp north at the old city of Chang'an; both were to come and receive his orders together.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Li Jiancheng to pick the finest grain-guard troops and hurry from Xinfeng to Changle Palace, while Li Shimin was to take the newly attached armies and encamp north at old Chang'an; both were to come and take his orders together.

sentences.zh: 延安、上郡、雕陰皆請降於淵。

translations.literal: Yan'an, Shangjun, and Diaoyin all asked to surrender to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan'an, Shang Commandery, and Diaoyin all offered submission to Li Yuan.

sentences.zh: 丙子，淵引軍西行，所過離宮園苑皆罷之，出宮女還其親屬。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi Yuan led his army west; wherever he passed, detached palaces and parklands were all shut down, and palace women were released to their kin.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingzi Li Yuan marched west. Every detached palace and park he passed was closed, and palace women were sent back to their families.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛巳，淵至長安，營於春明門之西北，諸軍皆集，合二十餘萬。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day xinsi, Yuan reached Chang'an and encamped northwest of the Spring Bright Gate; all armies gathered, totaling more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day xinsi, Li Yuan reached Chang'an and pitched camp northwest of the Spring Bright Gate. All forces assembled—more than two hundred thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 淵命各依壘壁，毋得入村落侵暴。

translations.literal: Yuan ordered each to abide by his ramparts and not enter villages to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan ordered every unit to keep to its walls and not enter villages to loot.

sentences.zh: 屢遣使至城下諭衛文升等以欲尊隋之意，不報。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys below the walls to inform Wei Wensheng and the others of his wish to uphold the Sui; they did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he sent envoys under the walls to tell Wei Wensheng and the rest that he meant to honor the Sui; they gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，命諸軍進圍城。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao he ordered all armies to advance and besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinmao he ordered the armies forward to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 甲午，淵遷館於安興坊。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu Yuan moved his lodging to Anxing Ward.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu Li Yuan moved his quarters to Anxing Ward.

sentences.zh: 巴陵校尉鄱陽董景珍、雷世猛、旅帥鄭文秀、許玄徹、萬瓚、徐德基、郭華、沔陽張繡等謀據郡叛隋，推景珍為主。

translations.literal: Dong Jingzhen of Poyang, a militia captain of Baling, Lei Shimeng, the expeditionary commander Zheng Wenxiu, Xu Xuance, Wan Chan, Xu Deji, Guo Hua, Zhang Xiu of Mianyang, and others plotted to hold the commandery and rebel against the Sui, proposing Jingzhen as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jingzhen of Poyang, a Baling militia captain, together with Lei Shimeng, the expeditionary commander Zheng Wenxiu, Xu Xuance, Wan Chan, Xu Deji, Guo Hua, Zhang Xiu of Mianyang, and others plotted to seize the commandery and break with the Sui, setting up Jingzhen as their head.

sentences.zh: 景珍曰：「吾素寒賤，不為眾所服。

translations.literal: Jingzhen said: "I have always been poor and lowly and am not obeyed by the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen said: "I have always been poor and obscure; the crowd will not follow me.

sentences.zh: 羅川令蕭銑，梁室之後，寬仁大度，請奉之以從眾望。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Luochuan, Xiao Xian, is a descendant of the House of Liang—magnanimous and broad-minded; I ask that we install him to follow the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian, magistrate of Luochuan, is of the House of Liang—generous and open-handed. Let us set him up to satisfy the people's wish.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使報銑。

translations.literal: " They then sent a messenger to inform Xian.
translations.idiomatic: They sent a messenger to tell Xiao Xian.

sentences.zh: 銑喜從之，聲言討賊，召募得數千人。

translations.literal: Xian gladly agreed; proclaiming that he was going to suppress bandits, he recruited several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian gladly assented. Proclaiming a campaign against bandits, he raised several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 銑，巖之孫也。

translations.literal: Xian was the grandson of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian was a grandson of Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 會穎川賊帥沈柳生寇羅川，銑與戰不利，因謂其眾曰：「今天下皆叛，隋政不行，巴陵豪傑起兵，欲奉吾為主。

translations.literal: Just then the bandit chief Shen Liusheng of Yingchuan raided Luochuan; Xian fought poorly and therefore said to his followers: "Today the whole realm is in revolt, Sui government no longer operates, and the heroes of Baling have raised troops wishing to install me as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Yingchuan bandit chief Shen Liusheng raided Luochuan. Xiao Xian fought poorly and told his men: "The whole empire is in revolt; Sui rule is dead. The heroes of Baling have risen and wish to make me their leader.

sentences.zh: 若從其請以號令江南，可以中興梁祚，以此召柳生，亦當從我矣。

translations.literal: " If I accept their request to command the south of the Yangtze, we can revive the fortune of Liang; with this I can summon Liusheng, and he too will follow me.
translations.idiomatic: If I accept and command the lands south of the Yangtze, we can restore the House of Liang. Summon Liusheng with that, and he will follow me too.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆悅，聽命，乃自稱梁公，改隋服色旗幟皆如梁舊。

translations.literal: " The crowd was pleased and obeyed; he then styled himself Duke of Liang and changed the Sui colors and banners to match the old Liang pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The men were pleased and obeyed. He styled himself Duke of Liang and changed robes, colors, and banners to the old Liang style.

sentences.zh: 柳生即帥眾歸之，以柳生為車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Liusheng at once led his followers to join him; Xian made Liusheng Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Liusheng at once brought his followers in. Xiao Xian made him Grand General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 起兵五日，遠近歸附者至數萬人，遂帥眾向巴陵。

translations.literal: Within five days of raising troops, those from near and far who came to attach themselves reached tens of thousands; he then led his army toward Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Five days after raising arms, adherents near and far had reached tens of thousands, and he marched on Baling.

sentences.zh: 景珍遣徐德基帥郡中豪傑數百人出迎，未及見銑，柳生與其黨謀曰：「我先奉梁公，勳居第一。

translations.literal: Jingzhen sent Xu Deji to lead several hundred leading men of the commandery out to welcome him; before Xian was met, Liusheng and his faction plotted: "I was the first to support the Duke of Liang; my merit ranks first.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen sent Xu Deji with several hundred commandery notables to welcome him. Before Xiao Xian appeared, Liusheng and his clique plotted: "I was first to raise the Duke of Liang; my merit stands first.

sentences.zh: 今巴陵諸將，皆位高兵多，我若入城，返出其下。

translations.literal: " Now the generals of Baling all outrank me and have more troops; if I enter the city, I will end up beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Baling commanders all outrank me and have larger forces. If I enter the city, I fall beneath them.

sentences.zh: 不如殺德基，質其首領，獨挾梁公進取郡城，則無出我右者矣。

translations.literal: " Better to kill Deji, seize their leaders as hostages, and alone hold the Duke of Liang to take the commandery city—then no one will rank above me.
translations.idiomatic: Better kill Deji, seize their chiefs as hostages, and alone hold the Duke of Liang to storm the commandery seat—then none will stand above me.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺德基。

translations.literal: " They then killed Deji.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Deji.

sentences.zh: 入白銑，銑大驚曰：「今欲撥亂反正，忽自相殺，吾不能為若主矣。

translations.literal: Reporting to Xian, Xian was greatly alarmed and said: "We now wish to settle chaos and restore order, yet suddenly we kill one another—I cannot be your ruler any longer.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported, Xiao Xian was appalled and said: "We mean to set the realm right, yet at once we butcher one another—I cannot be your lord.

sentences.zh: 」因步出軍門。

translations.literal: " He therefore walked out of the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: He walked out of the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 柳生大懼，伏地請罪，銑責而赦之，陳兵入城。

translations.literal: Liusheng was greatly afraid, prostrated himself and asked pardon; Xian rebuked but pardoned him and arrayed his troops to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liusheng was terrified, prostrated himself, and begged forgiveness. Xiao Xian rebuked but spared him and marched into the city in battle order.

sentences.zh: 景珍言於銑曰：「徐德基建義功臣，而柳生無故擅殺之，此而不誅，何以為政！

translations.literal: Jingzhen said to Xian: "Xu Deji was a founding merit holder; yet Liusheng killed him without cause—if this goes unpunished, how can there be government!
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen told Xiao Xian: "Xu Deji was a founding merit-holder, yet Liusheng murdered him without cause. If that goes unpunished, how can there be rule?

sentences.zh: 且柳生為盜日久，今雖從義，凶悖不移，共處一城，勢必為變。

translations.literal: " Moreover Liusheng has been a bandit for long; though he now follows the righteous cause, his fierce perversity is unchanged—sharing one city, strife is sure to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liusheng has been a bandit for years. Though he now follows the righteous cause, his brutish nature is unchanged. Under one roof, trouble is certain.

sentences.zh: 失今不取，後悔無及！

translations.literal: " Miss this chance and regrets will come too late!
translations.idiomatic: Miss this moment and regret will be endless!

sentences.zh: 」銑又從之。

translations.literal: " Xian again agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian agreed again.

sentences.zh: 景珍收柳生，斬之，其徒皆潰去。

translations.literal: Jingzhen seized Liusheng and beheaded him; his followers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen seized Liusheng and executed him; his men broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 丙申，銑築壇燔燎，自稱梁王，改元鳴鳳。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen Xian built an altar, offered burnt offerings, styled himself King of Liang, and changed the era name to Mingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingshen Xiao Xian built an altar, burned offerings, styled himself King of Liang, and proclaimed the era Mingfeng.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，王世充夜渡洛水，營於黑石，明日，分兵守營，自將精兵陳於洛北。

translations.literal: On the day renyin Wang Shichong crossed the Luo by night and encamped at Heishi; the next day he divided troops to hold the camp and himself led picked troops and drew up north of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin Wang Shichong crossed the Luo by night and encamped at Heishi. The next day he left a detachment to hold the camp and himself drew up picked troops north of the river.

sentences.zh: 李密聞之，引兵渡洛逆戰，密兵大敗，柴孝和溺死。

translations.literal: Li Mi heard of it and led his army across the Luo to meet him in battle; Mi's army was utterly defeated and Chai Xiaohe drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi heard and led his army across the Luo to meet him. Mi's force was shattered; Chai Xiaohe drowned.

sentences.zh: 密帥麾下精騎渡洛南，餘眾東走月城，世充追圍之。

translations.literal: Mi led his handpicked cavalry across to the south bank of the Luo; the rest of his force fled east to Yuecheng, and Shichong pursued and besieged them.
translations.idiomatic: Mi took his elite cavalry to the south bank; the rest fled east to Yuecheng, and Shichong pursued and besieged them.

sentences.zh: 密自洛南策馬直趣黑石，營中懼，連舉六烽，世充釋月城之圍，狼狽自救；

translations.literal: Mi from the south bank whipped his horse straight for Heishi; the camp was afraid and raised six signal fires in succession; Shichong lifted the siege of Yuecheng and fled in disarray to save himself;
translations.idiomatic: From the south bank Mi spurred straight for Heishi. The camp panicked and lit six beacon fires in a row. Shichong broke off the siege of Yuecheng and rushed back in disorder to save his camp;

sentences.zh: 密還與戰，大破之，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: Mi turned back and fought again, routing them utterly and taking more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Mi wheeled and struck again, crushing him and taking more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，李淵命諸攻城，約「毋得犯七廟及代王、宗室，違者夷三族！

translations.literal: On the day jiachen Li Yuan ordered a general assault on the city, stipulating: "You must not violate the seven ancestral temples, or the Prince of Dai, or the imperial clan—violators exterminate three generations!
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen Li Yuan ordered the armies to storm the city, on pain of death: "Do not touch the seven temples, the Prince of Dai, or the imperial clan—whoever violates this exterminates three generations!

sentences.zh: 」孫華中流矢卒。

translations.literal: " Sun Hua was struck by a stray arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hua was hit by a stray arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙辰，軍頭雷永吉先登，遂克長安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day bingchen, the assault leader Lei Yongji was first atop the wall; they thereupon captured Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day bingchen, the assault leader Lei Yongji was first on the wall, and Chang'an fell.

sentences.zh: 代王在東宮，左右奔散，唯侍讀姚思廉侍側。

translations.literal: The Prince of Dai was in the Eastern Palace; his attendants scattered and fled—only the Palace Reader Yao Silian waited at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Dai was in the Eastern Palace. Attendants scattered; only the Palace Reader Yao Silian remained at his side.

sentences.zh: 軍士將登殿，思廉厲聲訶之曰：「唐公舉義兵，匡帝室，卿等毋得無禮！

translations.literal: Soldiers were about to ascend the hall; Silian shouted them down in a stern voice: "Duke Tang has raised righteous troops to restore the imperial house—you must not be insolent!
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were about to mount the hall. Silian shouted them down: "Duke Tang has raised righteous troops to restore the throne—you must not be rude!

sentences.zh: 」眾皆愕然，布立庭下。

translations.literal: " The crowd were all stunned and stood in formation below the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The men stood stunned in ranks below the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 淵迎王於東宮，遷居大興殿後，聽思廉扶王至順陽閣下，泣拜而去。

translations.literal: Yuan welcomed the prince to the Eastern Palace and moved him to behind the Daxing Hall; he allowed Silian to support the prince down to below the Shunyang Pavilion, where Silian wept and bowed before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan received the prince at the Eastern Palace and moved him to quarters behind the Daxing Hall. He let Silian escort the prince down to the Shunyang Pavilion, where Silian wept, bowed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 思廉，察之子也。

translations.literal: Silian was the son of Cha.
translations.idiomatic: Silian was a son of Yao Cha.

sentences.zh: 淵還，捨於長樂宮，與民約法十二條，悉除隋苛禁。

translations.literal: Yuan returned and took up residence at Changle Palace; with the people he agreed on twelve articles of law, abolishing all of the Sui's harsh prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan returned and lodged at Changle Palace. With the people he agreed twelve articles of law and swept away the Sui's harsh bans.

sentences.zh: 淵之起兵也，留守官發其墳墓，毀其五廟。

translations.literal: When Yuan had raised his troops, the garrison officials had opened his ancestral tombs and destroyed his five temples.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan had first risen, the garrison officials had opened his ancestral graves and wrecked his five temples.

sentences.zh: 至是，衛文升已卒，戊午，執陰世師、骨儀等，數以貪婪苛酷，且拒義師，俱斬之，死者十餘人，餘無所問。

translations.literal: By this time Wei Wenkai had died; on the day wuwu they seized Yin Shishi, Gu Yi, and others, recounting their greed, cruelty, and refusal of the righteous army, and beheaded them all—more than ten dead; the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei Wenkai was dead. On the day wuwu they seized Yin Shishi, Gu Yi, and others, charged them with greed, cruelty, and resisting the righteous army, and beheaded them—more than ten in all; the rest went unprosecuted.

sentences.zh: 馬邑郡丞三原李靖，素與淵有隙，淵入城，將斬之。

translations.literal: Li Jing, assistant magistrate of Mayi commandery from Sanyuan, had long been at odds with Yuan; when Yuan entered the city he was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing of Sanyuan, assistant magistrate of Mayi, had long been at odds with Li Yuan. When Li Yuan entered the city he meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 靖大呼曰：「公興義兵，欲平暴亂，乃以私怨殺壯士乎！

translations.literal: Jing shouted: "You have raised righteous troops to quell violence and chaos—will you kill a stalwart man over a private grudge!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing cried out: "You have raised righteous troops to quell chaos—will you slay a able man over a private grudge?

sentences.zh: 」世民為之固請，乃捨之。

translations.literal: " Shimin pleaded firmly on his behalf, and so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin pleaded hard for him, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 世民因召置幕府。

translations.literal: Shimin then summoned him and placed him on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shimin then took him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 靖少負志氣，有文武才略，其舅韓擒虎每撫之曰：「可與言將帥之略者，獨此子耳！

translations.literal: Jing from youth had been ambitious, with both civil and military talent; his uncle Han Qinhu would stroke him and say: "The only one with whom one can discuss the art of command is this boy alone!
translations.idiomatic: From youth Li Jing was ambitious, skilled in civil and military arts alike. His uncle Han Qinhu would pat him and say: "Of all men, only this boy can talk strategy with me!

sentences.zh: 」王世充自洛北之敗，堅壁不出；

translations.literal: " After Shichong's defeat north of the Luo he held to his walls and would not come out;
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat north of the Luo, Wang Shichong shut himself in his walls and would not come out;

sentences.zh: 越王侗遣使勞之，世充慚懼，請戰於密。

translations.literal: the Prince of Yue Tong sent envoys to encourage him; Shichong, ashamed and afraid, requested battle with Mi.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent envoys to encourage him. Shichong, ashamed and afraid, asked to fight Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，世充與密夾石子河而陳，密佈陳南北十餘里，翟讓先與世充戰，不利而退；

translations.literal: On the day bingchen Shichong and Mi faced each other across the Shizi River; Mi drew up his battle line for more than ten li north and south; Zhai Rang first fought Shichong and, doing poorly, withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen Shichong and Mi faced each other across the Shizi River. Mi arrayed his line for more than ten li north and south. Zhai Rang engaged Shichong first, fared badly, and fell back;

sentences.zh: 世充逐之，王伯當、裴仁基從旁橫斷其後，密勒中軍擊之，世充大敗，西走。

translations.literal: Shichong pursued him; Wang Baidang and Pei Renji cut off his rear from the flank; Mi drove the center army against him; Shichong was utterly defeated and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong pursued. Wang Baidang and Pei Renji struck his rear from the flank. Mi drove the center against him. Shichong was routed and fled west.

sentences.zh: 翟讓司馬王儒信勸讓自為大塚宰，總統眾務，以奪密權，讓不從。

translations.literal: Zhai Rang's aide Wang Ruxin urged Rang to make himself Grand Prime Minister and oversee all affairs, thereby seizing Mi's power; Rang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Rang's aide Wang Ruxin urged Rang to make himself Grand Prime Minister, take all affairs in hand, and strip Li Mi of power. Rang refused.

sentences.zh: 讓兄柱國滎陽公弘，粗愚人也，謂讓曰：「天子汝當自為，奈何與人！

translations.literal: Rang's elder brother Hong, the Duke of Yingyang and pillar of state—a coarse, foolish man—said to Rang: "The Son of Heaven—you should take it yourself; why hand it to another!
translations.idiomatic: Rang's elder brother Hong, Duke of Yingyang and a pillar of state—a coarse, stupid man—said to him: "The Son of Heaven is yours to be—why give it to someone else?

sentences.zh: 汝不為者，我當為之！

translations.literal: If you will not do it, I shall do it!
translations.idiomatic: If you will not take it, I shall!

sentences.zh: 」讓但大笑，不以為意，密聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Rang only laughed greatly and paid it no mind; Mi heard of it and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Rang only laughed it off. When Mi heard, he took it ill.

sentences.zh: 總管崔世樞自鄢陵初附於密，讓囚之私府，責其貨，世樞營求未辦，遽欲加刑。

translations.literal: Director-General Cui Shishu, who had first submitted from Yanling to Mi, Rang imprisoned in his private residence and demanded his goods; Shishu had not yet raised what was sought when Rang suddenly wished to impose punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Director-General Cui Shishu had lately come over from Yanling to Li Mi. Zhai Rang locked him in his private quarters and demanded a payoff. Before Shishu could raise the sum, Rang was ready to punish him.

sentences.zh: 讓召元帥府記室邢義期博，逡巡未就，杖之八十。

translations.literal: Rang summoned marshal headquarters recorder Xing Yiqi to gamble; he hesitated and did not come—Rang had him beaten eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Rang summoned the marshal's recorder Xing Yiqi for a game of chance. When Xing delayed and did not appear, Rang had him flogged eighty strokes.

sentences.zh: 讓謂左長史房彥藻曰：「君前破汝南，大得寶貨，獨與魏公，全不與我！

translations.literal: Rang said to Left Chief Clerk Fang Yanzao: "When you earlier took Runan, you gained great treasure and gave it all to the Duke of Wei, none to me!
translations.idiomatic: Rang told Left Chief Clerk Fang Yanzao: "When you took Runan you seized a great haul of treasure and gave every bit to the Duke of Wei—not a scrap to me!

sentences.zh: 魏公我之所立，事未可知。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei is one I raised up; how things will turn out is not yet known.
translations.idiomatic: I made the Duke of Wei what he is. How this ends is still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 」彥藻懼，以狀告密，因與左司馬鄭頲共說密曰：「讓貪愎不仁，有無君之心，宜早圖之。

translations.literal: Yanzao was afraid and reported the situation to Mi; together with Left Major Zheng Ting he urged Mi, saying: "Rang is greedy, obstinate, and without benevolence, and has a heart that disowns his lord—you should plot against him early."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzao, alarmed, reported everything to Li Mi. He and Left Major Zheng Ting then urged Mi together: "Rang is greedy, brutal, and disloyal. He already acts like a ruler in his own right. You should deal with him soon."

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「今安危未定，遽相誅殺，何以示遠！

translations.literal: Mi said: "Now safety and peril are not yet settled; to kill one another in haste—how would that look to those far away!"
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Our position is still unsettled. If we turn to slaughter now, what will men far away think of us?"

sentences.zh: 」頲曰：「毒蛇螫手，壯士解腕，所全者大故也。

translations.literal: Ting said: "When a poisonous snake bites the hand, the stalwart man cuts off his wrist—the greater whole is what is preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Ting said: "When a viper strikes the hand, a brave man severs the wrist to save the rest of the body."

sentences.zh: 彼先得志，悔無所及。

translations.literal: If he gains his aim first, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Let him get there first and you will have no chance to repent.

sentences.zh: 」密乃從之，置酒召讓。

translations.literal: Mi then followed his advice and set out wine to summon Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Mi took his counsel, laid a feast, and summoned Rang.

sentences.zh: 戊午，讓與兄弘及兄子司徒府長史摩侯同詣密，密與讓、弘、裴仁基、郝孝德共坐，單雄信等皆立侍，房彥藻、鄭頲往來檢校。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Rang with his elder brother Hong and his brother's son Mo Hou, chief clerk of the Steward of Masters' office, went together to Mi; Mi sat with Rang, Hong, Pei Renji, and Hao Xiaode, while Shan Xiongxin and others all stood in attendance, and Fang Yanzao and Zheng Ting went back and forth inspecting.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Zhai Rang came with his brother Hong and his nephew Mo Hou, chief clerk in the Steward of Masters' office. Li Mi sat with Rang, Hong, Pei Renji, and Hao Xiaode. Shan Xiongxin and the rest stood by. Fang Yanzao and Zheng Ting moved about, keeping watch.

sentences.zh: 密曰：「今日與達官飲，不須多人，左右止留數人給使而已。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Today we drink with eminent officials—no need for many men; retain only a few attendants to serve."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Today is a feast with our leaders. We need few men about—only a handful of attendants."

sentences.zh: 」密左右皆引去，讓左右猶在。

translations.literal: Mi's attendants were all led away; Rang's attendants still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's guards were sent away. Rang's men remained.

sentences.zh: 彥藻白密曰：「今方為樂，天時甚寒，司徒左右，請給酒食。

translations.literal: Yanzao reported to Mi: "We are at our revelry and the weather is very cold—the Steward's attendants should be given wine and food."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzao said to Mi: "We are feasting and the day is bitterly cold. The Steward's men should have wine and food."

sentences.zh: 」密曰：「聽司徒進止。

translations.literal: Mi said: "Let the Steward decide."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "Let the Steward say."

sentences.zh: 」讓應曰：「甚佳。

translations.literal: Rang answered: "Excellent."
translations.idiomatic: Rang said: "Very well."

sentences.zh: 」乃引讓左右盡出，獨密下壯士蔡建德持刀立侍。

translations.literal: Then Rang's attendants were all led out; only Mi's stalwart Cai Jiande stood in attendance holding a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's men were then led out as well. Only Cai Jiande, a warrior in Mi's service, stood by with a blade in hand.

sentences.zh: 食未進，密出良弓，與讓習射，讓方引滿，建德自後斫之，踣於床前，聲若牛吼，並弘、摩侯、儒信皆殺之。

translations.literal: Before food was served, Mi produced a fine bow and practiced archery with Rang; as Rang was drawing to the full, Jiande struck him from behind—he fell before the couch with a sound like an ox roaring—and Hong, Mo Hou, and Ruxin were all killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Before the meal was served Mi brought out a fine bow and invited Rang to practice. As Rang drew the string to the full, Jiande struck from behind. Rang crashed before the couch with a roar like a bull. Hong, Mo Hou, and Wang Ruxin were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 徐世勣走出，門者斫之傷頸，王伯當遙訶止之。

translations.literal: Xu Shiji ran out; the gate guards hacked him and wounded his neck; Wang Bodang shouted from afar and stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shiji fled. Guards at the gate slashed his neck. Wang Bodang shouted from a distance and made them stop.

sentences.zh: 單雄信叩頭請命，密釋之。

translations.literal: Shan Xiongxin kowtowed begging for his life; Mi released him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Xiongxin kowtowed for mercy. Mi spared him.

sentences.zh: 左右驚擾，莫知所為，密大言曰：「與君等同起義兵，本除暴亂。

translations.literal: The attendants were alarmed and in turmoil, not knowing what to do; Mi spoke loudly: "I rose in arms together with you all to end tyranny and chaos."
translations.idiomatic: The hall erupted in confusion. Mi cried out: "We took up arms together to end tyranny and chaos."

sentences.zh: 司徒專行貪虐，陵辱群僚，無復上下；

translations.literal: The Steward alone practiced greed and cruelty, insulting the whole staff of officials, with no more distinction between superior and subordinate;
translations.idiomatic: The Steward alone was greedy and cruel. He humiliated every officer and erased all rank between high and low.

sentences.zh: 今所誅止其一家，諸君無預也。

translations.literal: what is executed now is only his household—you gentlemen have no part in it.
translations.idiomatic: What we have killed is only his household. None of you are implicated.

sentences.zh: 」命扶徐世勣置幕下，親為傅創。

translations.literal: He ordered Xu Shiji supported and placed beneath the canopy, and personally applied medicine to his wound.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xu Shiji carried to his tent and dressed the wound himself.

sentences.zh: 讓麾下欲散，密使單雄信前往宣慰，密尋獨騎入其營，歷加撫諭，令世勣、雄信、伯當分領其眾，中外遂定。

translations.literal: Rang's followers wished to disperse; Mi sent Shan Xiongxin forward to announce comfort; Mi soon entered their camp alone on horseback, going through and offering reassurance, ordering Shiji, Xiongxin, and Bodang each to take command of part of the host, and within and without were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Rang's troops were on the verge of breaking up. Mi sent Shan Xiongxin to reassure them, then rode alone into their camp and spoke to each company in turn. He put Shiji, Xiongxin, and Bodang in charge of Rang's men. Order was restored inside and out.

sentences.zh: 讓殘忍，摩侯猜忌，儒信貪縱，故死之日，所部無哀之者；

translations.literal: Rang was cruel, Mo Hou suspicious, and Ruxin greedy and unrestrained—therefore on the day they died none of those under them mourned;
translations.idiomatic: Rang had been cruel, Mo Hou suspicious, Ruxin greedy and dissolute. When they died, none of their followers grieved.

sentences.zh: 然密之將佐始有自疑之心矣。

translations.literal: yet Mi's generals and aides now first had hearts that doubted themselves.
translations.idiomatic: But from that day Mi's own officers began to doubt whether they were safe with him.

sentences.zh: 始，王世充知讓與密必不久睦，冀其相圖，得從而乘之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Shichong knew Rang and Mi would surely not long remain friendly, and hoped they would plot against each other so he could take advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong had long known that Zhai Rang and Li Mi could not remain allies for long. He hoped they would destroy each other so he could strike at the survivor.

sentences.zh: 及聞讓死，大失望，歎曰：「李密天資明決，為龍為蛇，固不可測也！

translations.literal: When he heard Rang was dead he was greatly disappointed and sighed: "Li Mi's natural gifts are bright and decisive—whether dragon or serpent, he truly cannot be fathomed!"
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Rang was dead he was deeply disappointed and sighed: "Li Mi is brilliant and resolute. Whether he proves a dragon or a serpent, no one can tell."

sentences.zh: 壬戌，李淵備法駕迎代王即皇帝位於天興殿，時年十三，大赦，改元，遙尊煬帝為太上皇。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Li Yuan prepared the imperial equipage to welcome the Prince of Dai to take the imperial throne in the Hall of Heavenly Felicity; he was thirteen years old; a great amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed, and Emperor Yang was honored from afar as Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day Li Yuan brought out the imperial regalia and had the Prince of Dai enthroned in the Hall of Heavenly Felicity. The boy was thirteen. A general amnesty was declared, the reign title was changed, and Emperor Yang was acknowledged from afar as Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲子，淵自長樂宮入長安。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Yuan entered Chang'an from Everlasting Joy Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Yuan entered Chang'an from Everlasting Joy Palace.

sentences.zh: 以淵為假黃鉞、使持節、大都督內外諸軍事、尚書令、大丞相，進封唐王。

translations.literal: Yuan was made Acting Grand Chancellor, bearer of the staff of authority, Grand Commander of all military affairs within and without, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Chancellor, and advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was appointed Acting Grand Chancellor, bearer of the staff of authority, supreme commander of all forces at home and abroad, Director of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Chancellor, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 以武德殿為丞相府，改教稱令，日於虔化門視事。

translations.literal: The Hall of Martial Virtue was made the Grand Chancellor's residence; edicts were renamed orders; daily he conducted affairs at the Gate of Sincere Transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Martial Virtue became the chancellor's headquarters. Edicts were restyled as orders. Each day he held court at the Gate of Sincere Transformation.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，榆林、靈武、平涼、安定諸郡皆遣使請命。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, the commanderies of Yulin, Lingwu, Pingliang, and Anding all sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day the commanderies of Yulin, Lingwu, Pingliang, and Anding all sent envoys to pledge allegiance.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔軍國機務，事無大小，文武設官，位無貴賤，憲章賞罰，鹹歸相府；

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, an edict declared that military and state affairs, matters great and small, civil and military appointments, posts high and low, laws and rewards and punishments—all were to return to the chancellor's office;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day an edict placed all military and civil business, appointments high and low, and the power to reward and punish in the hands of the chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 唯郊祀天地，四時禘示合奏聞。

translations.literal: only suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the seasonal di and shi rites were to be reported jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Only suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth and the seasonal ancestral rites were to be reported to the throne jointly.

sentences.zh: 置丞相府官屬，以裴寂為長史，劉文靜為司馬。

translations.literal: The chancellor's staff was established, with Pei Ji as chief clerk and Liu Wenjing as major.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor's staff was formed, with Pei Ji as chief clerk and Liu Wenjing as major.

sentences.zh: 何潘仁使李綱入見，淵留之，以專掌選事。

translations.literal: He Panren had Li Gang come in audience; Yuan retained him to oversee selection of officials exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: He Panren sent Li Gang to an audience. Yuan kept him in charge of appointments.

sentences.zh: 又以前考功郎中竇威為司錄參軍，使定禮儀。

translations.literal: Also the former Director of Merit Review Dou Wei was made registrar aide and charged to fix ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He also named the former Director of Merit Review Dou Wei registrar aide and set him to codify court ritual.

sentences.zh: 威，熾之子也。

translations.literal: Wei was the son of Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Wei was the son of Dou Chi.

sentences.zh: 淵傾府庫以賜勳人，國用不足，右光祿大夫劉世龍獻策，以為「今義師數萬，並在京師，樵蘇貴而布帛賤；

translations.literal: Yuan emptied the treasury to reward men of merit; state funds were insufficient; Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Liu Shilong offered a plan, saying: "Now the righteous army numbers tens of thousands, all in the capital; firewood is costly while cloth is cheap;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan emptied the treasury rewarding his followers, and the treasury ran dry. Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Liu Shilong proposed: "Tens of thousands of our troops are in the capital. Firewood is dear and cloth is cheap.

sentences.zh: 請伐六街及苑中樹為樵，以易布帛，可得數十萬匹。

translations.literal: I ask to cut the trees of the six avenues and the imperial park for fuel, exchange them for cloth, and thus obtain several hundred thousand bolts."
translations.idiomatic: Cut the trees along the six main avenues and in the imperial park for fuel, trade the wood for cloth, and we can obtain several hundred thousand bolts."

sentences.zh: 」淵從之。

translations.literal: Yuan followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以李建成為唐世子，李世民為京兆尹、秦公，李元吉為齊公。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Li Jiancheng was made Heir of Tang, Li Shimin was made Intendant of Jingzhao and Duke of Qin, and Li Yuanji was made Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day Li Jiancheng was named Heir of Tang, Li Shimin Intendant of Jingzhao and Duke of Qin, and Li Yuanji Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 河南諸郡盡附李密，唯滎陽太守郇王慶、梁郡太守楊汪尚為隋守。

translations.literal: The commanderies of Henan all submitted to Li Mi; only Yingyang Prefect Xun Wang Qing and Liang commandery Prefect Yang Wang still held for Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Every commandery in Henan had submitted to Li Mi except Yingyang, where Prefect Xun Wang Qing still held for Sui, and Liang, where Prefect Yang Wang did the same.

sentences.zh: 密以書招慶，為陳厲害，且曰：「王之先世，本住山東，本姓郭氏，乃非楊族。

translations.literal: Mi sent a letter to recruit Qing, setting forth harm and benefit, and also said: "Your lordship's forebears originally dwelt in Shandong; your original surname was Guo—you are not of the Yang clan."
translations.idiomatic: Mi wrote inviting Qing to submit, laying out the stakes, and added: "Your ancestors came from Shandong. Your true surname is Guo. You are no Yang clansman."

sentences.zh: 芝焚蕙歎，事不同此。

translations.literal: When the orchid is burned the sweet flag sighs—this matter is not the same.
translations.idiomatic: When the orchid burns, the sweet flag sighs beside it—but your case is not that one.

sentences.zh: 」初，慶祖父元孫早孤，隨母郭氏養於舅族。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qing's grandfather Yuansun was orphaned young and was raised among his mother's Guo kin by her clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qing's grandfather Yuansun had lost his father young and was raised among his mother's Guo relatives.

sentences.zh: 及武元帝從周文帝起兵關中，元孫在鄴，恐為高氏所誅，冒姓郭氏，故密云然。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou followed Emperor Wen of Zhou in raising troops in Guanzhong, Yuansun was in Ye and, fearing execution by the Gao clan, took the surname Guo falsely—hence Mi's letter spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou followed Zhou Wendi in raising arms in Guanzhong, Yuansun was in Ye. Fearing the Gao clan would kill him, he took the surname Guo. That was why Mi wrote as he did.

sentences.zh: 慶得書惶恐，即以郡降密，複姓郭氏。

translations.literal: Qing received the letter in fear and at once surrendered the commandery to Mi, resuming the surname Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was terrified by the letter, surrendered the commandery at once, and resumed the surname Guo.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸未，追謚唐王淵大父襄公為景王；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day guiwei, posthumous titles were granted: the Prince of Tang Yuan's great-grandfather Duke Xiang was titled King Jing;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guiwei day, posthumous honors were granted: Yuan's great-grandfather, Duke Xiang, was titled King Jing.

sentences.zh: 考仁公為元王，夫人竇氏為穆妃。

translations.literal: his father Duke Ren was titled King Yuan, and Lady Dou was titled Consort Mu.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Duke Ren, was titled King Yuan, and Lady Dou was named Consort Mu.

sentences.zh: 薛舉遣其子仁果寇扶風，唐弼據汧源拒之。

translations.literal: Xue Ju sent his son Renguo to raid Fufeng; Tang Bi held Qianyuan and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju sent his son Renguo against Fufeng. Tang Bi held Qianyuan and barred the way.

sentences.zh: 舉遣使招弼，弼乃殺李弘芝，請降於舉，仁果乘其無備，襲破之，悉並其眾。

translations.literal: Ju sent an envoy to win Bi; Bi then killed Li Hongzhi and asked to submit to Ju; Renguo, catching him unprepared, struck and broke him and wholly absorbed his host.
translations.idiomatic: Ju sent envoys to win Tang Bi over. Bi killed Li Hongzhi and offered to submit. Renguo caught him off guard, routed him, and absorbed his entire force.

sentences.zh: 弼以數百騎走詣扶風請降，扶風太守竇璡殺之。

translations.literal: Bi fled with several hundred horsemen to Fufeng to submit; Fufeng Prefect Dou Jin killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi fled with a few hundred horsemen to Fufeng to surrender. Prefect Dou Jin had him killed.

sentences.zh: 舉勢益張，眾號三十萬，謀取長安；

translations.literal: Ju's power grew ever greater; his host was said to number three hundred thousand, and he plotted to take Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: Ju's power swelled. His army was said to number three hundred thousand men, and he aimed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 聞丞相淵已定長安，遂圍扶風。

translations.literal: hearing that Grand Chancellor Yuan had already secured Chang'an, he then besieged Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Chancellor Yuan had already taken Chang'an, he laid siege to Fufeng instead.

sentences.zh: 淵使李世民將兵擊之。

translations.literal: Yuan sent Li Shimin to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Li Shimin to attack him.

sentences.zh: 又使姜謨、竇軌俱出散關，安撫隴右；

translations.literal: He also sent Jiang Mo and Dou Gui together out through Sanshui Pass to pacify Longyou;
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Jiang Mo and Dou Gui through Sanshui Pass to pacify Longyou.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫李孝恭招慰山南；

translations.literal: Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Xiaogong was to win over the south of the mountains;
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Li Xiaogong was to win over the lands south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 府戶曹張道源招慰山東。

translations.literal: the headquarters registrar Zhang Daoyuan was to win over Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters registrar Zhang Daoyuan was to win over Shandong.

sentences.zh: 孝恭，淵之從父兄子也。

translations.literal: Xiaogong was the son of Yuan's father's elder brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong was a cousin of Yuan's generation.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，世民擊薛仁果於扶風，大破之，追奔至□坻而還。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Shimin attacked Xue Renguo at Fufeng and routed him greatly, pursuing in flight to Gaozhi and returning.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Shimin met Xue Renguo at Fufeng and shattered his army, pursuing as far as Gaozhi before turning back.

sentences.zh: 薛舉大懼，問其群臣曰：「自古天子有降事乎？

translations.literal: Xue Ju was greatly afraid and asked his ministers: "Since antiquity has any Son of Heaven had occasion to submit?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ju was badly shaken and asked his ministers: "Has any Son of Heaven in history ever surrendered?"

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎錢唐褚亮曰：「趙佗歸漢，劉禪仕晉，近世蕭琮，至今猶貴。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary Chu Liang of Qiantang said: "Zhao Tuo submitted to Han, Liu Shan served Jin, and in recent times Xiao Cong—each remains honored to this day."
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant-in-ordinary Chu Liang of Qiantang said: "Zhao Tuo submitted to Han. Liu Shan served Jin. In our own day Xiao Cong still enjoys rank and honor."

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，自古有之。

translations.literal: Turning calamity into blessing has existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Turning disaster into fortune is nothing new in history.

sentences.zh: 」衛尉卿郝瑗趨進曰：「陛下失問！

translations.literal: Minister of the Guard Hao Yuan hurried forward and said: "Your Majesty has asked amiss!"
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Guard Hao Yuan stepped forward sharply and said: "Your Majesty has asked the wrong question!"

sentences.zh: 褚亮之言又何悖也！

translations.literal: How perverse are Chu Liang's words!
translations.idiomatic: What nonsense is Chu Liang talking!

sentences.zh: 昔漢高祖屢經奔敗，蜀先主亟亡妻子，卒成大業；

translations.literal: Formerly Gaodi of Han was repeatedly driven to flight in defeat, and the Former Lord of Shu often lost wife and children, yet in the end each achieved the great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: "Gaodi of Han was routed again and again. The Former Lord of Shu lost his family more than once. Each still won the realm in the end.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何以一戰不利，遽為亡國之計乎！

translations.literal: how can Your Majesty, on one battle going ill, hastily adopt plans for a perished state!"
translations.idiomatic: How can you, after a single defeat, talk at once of surrendering your state!"

sentences.zh: 」舉亦悔之，曰：「聊以此試君等耳。

translations.literal: Ju also regretted it and said: "I was merely testing you gentlemen for the moment."
translations.idiomatic: Ju regretted the question and said: "I was only testing you."

sentences.zh: 」乃厚賞瑗，引為謀主。

translations.literal: He then richly rewarded Yuan and drew him in as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded Hao Yuan lavishly and made him his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 乙未，平涼留守張隆，丁酉，河池太守蕭瑀及扶風漢陽郡相繼來降。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Pingliang garrison commander Zhang Long; on the day dingyou, Hechi Prefect Xiao Yu and Fufeng and Hanyang commanderies came to submit in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day Zhang Long, garrison commander of Pingliang, submitted. On dingyou day Prefect Xiao Yu of Hechi came over, followed by Fufeng and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 以竇璡為工部尚書、燕國公，蕭瑀為禮部尚書、宋國公。

translations.literal: Dou Jin was made Minister of Works and Duke of Yan, and Xiao Yu was made Minister of Rites and Duke of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jin was appointed Minister of Works and Duke of Yan. Xiao Yu was appointed Minister of Rites and Duke of Song.

sentences.zh: 姜謨、竇軌進至長道，為薛舉所敗，引還。

translations.literal: Jiang Mo and Dou Gui advanced to Changdao, were defeated by Xue Ju, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Mo and Dou Gui advanced to Changdao, were beaten by Xue Ju, and fell back.

sentences.zh: 淵使通議大夫醴泉劉世讓安集唐弼餘黨，與舉相遇，戰敗，為舉所虜。

translations.literal: Yuan sent Master of Comprehensive Discussion Liu Shirang of Liquan to settle the remnant band of Tang Bi; he met Ju in battle, was defeated, and was captured by Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Master of Comprehensive Discussion Liu Shirang of Liquan to pacify Tang Bi's remnant followers. He met Xue Ju in battle, was defeated, and taken captive.

sentences.zh: 李孝恭擊破朱粲，諸將請盡殺其俘，孝恭曰：「不可，自是以往，誰復肯降矣！

translations.literal: Li Xiaogong defeated Zhu Can; the generals asked to kill all the captives; Xiaogong said: "It cannot be done—from now on who would be willing to submit!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaogong routed Zhu Can. His officers asked to kill every captive. Xiaogong said: "No. If we do that, who will ever surrender again?"

sentences.zh: 」皆釋之。

translations.literal: All were released.
translations.idiomatic: He released them all.

sentences.zh: 於是自金川出巴、蜀，檄書所至，降附者三十餘州。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Jinchuan he issued into Ba and Shu; wherever his proclamations reached, more than thirty provinces submitted.
translations.idiomatic: From Jinchuan he moved into Ba and Shu. Wherever his proclamations arrived, more than thirty provinces submitted.

sentences.zh: 屈突通與劉文靜相持月餘，通復使桑顯和夜襲其營，文靜與左光祿大夫段志玄悉力苦戰，顯和敗走，盡俘其眾，通勢益蹙。
