translations.literal: Qu Tu Tong and Liu Wenjing faced each other for more than a month; Tong again had Sang Xianhe raid the camp by night; Wenjing and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Duan Zhixuan fought with all their strength in bitter combat; Xianhe was defeated and fled, and all his host was captured; Tong's situation grew ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tu Tong and Liu Wenjing had faced each other for more than a month. Tong again sent Sang Xianhe to raid the camp by night. Wenjing and Left Grand Master Duan Zhixuan fought desperately. Xianhe was routed and his entire force captured. Tong's position grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 或說通降，通泣曰：「吾歷事兩主，恩顧甚厚。

translations.literal: Some urged Tong to submit; Tong wept and said: "I have served two rulers in succession; their grace toward me was very deep."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Qu Tu Tong to surrender. He wept and said: "I have served two emperors in succession, and both showed me great favor."

sentences.zh: 食人之祿而違其難，吾不為也！

translations.literal: To eat a man's salary and betray him in his hardship—I will not do it!"
translations.idiomatic: I will not eat a lord's grain and abandon him in his hour of need!"

sentences.zh: 」每自摩其頸曰：「要當為國家受一刀！

translations.literal: Each time he would stroke his own neck and say: "I must yet take a blade for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: He would stroke his own neck and say: "Sooner or later I must take the state's blade upon it!"

sentences.zh: 」勞勉將士，未嘗不流涕，人亦以此懷之。

translations.literal: In encouraging the officers and men he never failed to shed tears, and men for this reason were attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he exhorted his troops he wept every time, and they loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 丞相淵遣其家僮召之，通立斬之。

translations.literal: Grand Chancellor Yuan sent his household servant to summon him; Tong at once beheaded the man.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Yuan sent a household servant to summon him. Tong beheaded the messenger on the spot.

sentences.zh: 及聞長安不守，家屬悉為淵所虜，乃留顯和鎮潼關，引兵東出，將趣洛陽。

translations.literal: When he heard Chang'an was lost and his family were all captured by Yuan, he left Xianhe to hold Tong Pass and led troops east, intending to make for Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Chang'an had fallen and his family were Yuan's prisoners, he left Xianhe to hold Tong Pass and marched east toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 通適去，顯和即以城降文靜。

translations.literal: Tong had just departed when Xianhe at once surrendered the city to Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Tong left when Xianhe surrendered the city to Liu Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 文靜遣竇琮等將輕騎與顯和追之，及於稠桑。

translations.literal: Wenjing sent Dou Cong and others to lead light cavalry with Xianhe in pursuit, catching up at Chousang.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing sent Dou Cong and others with light cavalry and Xianhe in pursuit. They overtook Tong at Chousang.

sentences.zh: 通結陳自固，竇琮遣通子壽往諭之。

translations.literal: Tong arrayed his ranks and held firm; Dou Cong sent Tong's son Shou to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong drew up his battle line and held his ground. Dou Cong sent Tong's son Shou to reason with him.

sentences.zh: 通罵曰：「此賊何來！

translations.literal: Tong cursed: "Whence comes this rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Tong roared: "What traitor is this!"

sentences.zh: 昔與汝為父子，今與汝為仇讎！

translations.literal: Formerly I was father to you; now I am your deadly foe!"
translations.idiomatic: Once I was your father. Now you are my enemy!"

sentences.zh: 」命左右射之。

translations.literal: He ordered those at his side to shoot him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his men to shoot at him.

sentences.zh: 顯和謂其眾曰：「今京城已陷，汝輩皆關中人，去欲何之！

translations.literal: Xianhe said to his host: "Now the capital has fallen—you are all men of Guanzhong; where do you think you are going!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe called to Tong's troops: "The capital is lost. You are all men of Guanzhong. Where do you imagine you are going?"

sentences.zh: 」眾皆釋仗而降。

translations.literal: The host all cast aside weapons and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: They laid down their arms and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 通知不免，下馬，東南再拜號哭曰：「臣力屈至此，非敢負國，天地神示氏實知之！

translations.literal: Tong knew he could not escape; he dismounted, bowed twice toward the southeast, and wailed: "Your servant's strength is broken to this point—I dare not betray the state; heaven and earth and the spirits truly know it!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing there was no escape, Tong dismounted, bowed twice toward the southeast, and wailed: "I am broken, not faithless. Heaven and earth and the spirits know it!"

sentences.zh: 」軍人執通送長安，淵以為兵部尚書，賜爵蔣公，兼秦公元帥府長史。

translations.literal: Soldiers seized Tong and sent him to Chang'an; Yuan made him Minister of War, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiang, and also appointed him chief clerk of the Duke of Qin's marshal headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers seized Tong and brought him to Chang'an. Yuan appointed him Minister of War, enfeoffed him as Duke of Jiang, and named him chief clerk on the Duke of Qin's staff.

sentences.zh: 淵遣通至河東城下招諭堯君素，君素見通，歔欷不自勝，通亦泣下沾衿，因謂君素曰：「吾軍已敗，義旗所指，莫不響應，事勢如此，卿當早降。

translations.literal: Yuan sent Tong to the walls of Hedong to summon and persuade Yao Junsu; Junsu saw Tong and sobbed beyond control; Tong also wept until his collar was wet and therefore said to Junsu: "Our army is already defeated; wherever the banner of righteousness points, none fail to answer—matters stand thus; you should submit early."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan sent Tong to Hedong to persuade Yao Junsu to surrender. When Junsu saw him he sobbed uncontrollably. Tong wept until his collar was soaked and said: "Our army is beaten. Every city answers the banner of righteousness. You should submit while you can."

sentences.zh: 」君素曰：「公為國大臣，主上委公以關中，代王付公以社稷，奈何負國生降，乃更為人作說客邪！

translations.literal: Junsu said: "You are a great minister of state; the emperor entrusted you with Guanzhong, and the Prince of Dai entrusted you with the altars of soil and grain—how can you betray the state and live in submission, and then moreover act as another man's persuader!"
translations.idiomatic: Junsu said: "You are a pillar of the state. The emperor entrusted Guanzhong to you. The Prince of Dai entrusted the realm to you. How can you betray your country, save your skin, and then come back as another man's mouthpiece?"

sentences.zh: 公所乘馬，即代王所賜也，公何面目乘之哉！

translations.literal: The horse you ride is the very one Prince Dai bestowed—how can you bear to mount it!
translations.idiomatic: The horse you ride is the very one Prince Dai gave you—how can you face riding it!

sentences.zh: 」通曰：「吁！

translations.literal: Tong said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Qutu Tong said: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 君素，我力屈而來。

translations.literal: Junsu, I have come because my strength is spent."
translations.idiomatic: Junsu, I have come because I am at the end of my strength."

sentences.zh: 」君素曰：「方今力猶未屈，何用多言！

translations.literal: Junsu said: "Your strength is not yet spent—what need for so many words!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Junsu said: "Your strength is not yet spent—why say so much!

sentences.zh: 」通慚而退。

translations.literal: Tong withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Qutu Tong withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 東都米斗三千，人餓死者什二三。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital rice was three thousand cash per dou; of the people, one or two in ten died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang rice cost three thousand cash per dou, and one or two people in ten starved to death.

sentences.zh: 庚子，王世充軍士有亡降李密者，密問：「世充軍中何所為？

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, some of Wang Shichong's soldiers deserted to Li Mi; Mi asked: "What is Shichong's army doing?
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengzi, some of Wang Shichong's soldiers deserted to Li Mi. Mi asked: "What is Shichong's army up to?

sentences.zh: 」軍士曰：「比見益募兵，再饗將士，不知其故。

translations.literal: The soldier said: "Lately I have seen them recruiting more troops and twice feasting the officers and men—I do not know why."
translations.idiomatic: The soldier said: "Lately they have been recruiting more troops and twice feasting the officers and men. I do not know why."

sentences.zh: 」密謂裴仁基曰：「吾幾落奴度中，光祿知之乎？

translations.literal: Mi said to Pei Renji: "I nearly fell into that slave's trap—do you understand, Director of Ceremonies?
translations.idiomatic: Mi said to Pei Renji: "I nearly fell into that slave's trap—do you see it, Director of Ceremonies?

sentences.zh: 吾久不出兵，世充芻糧將竭，求戰不得，故募兵饗士，欲乘月晦以襲倉城耳，宜速備之。

translations.literal: I have long kept my army in camp; Shichong's fodder and grain are nearly exhausted and he cannot obtain battle, so he recruits troops and feasts his men, intending to use the dark of the moon to strike the granary city—that is all; we should prepare quickly."
translations.idiomatic: I have kept my army idle so long that Shichong's supplies are nearly gone and he cannot get a battle. That is why he is recruiting and feasting his men—he means to strike the granary city under cover of the dark moon. We must prepare at once."

sentences.zh: 」乃命平原公郝孝德、琅邪公王伯當、齊郡公孟讓勒兵分屯倉城之側以待之。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Duke of Pingyuan Hao Xiaode, the Duke of Langye Wang Bodang, and the Duke of Qi Meng Rang to lead troops and encamp on either side of the granary city to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Duke of Pingyuan Hao Xiaode, the Duke of Langye Wang Bodang, and the Duke of Qi Meng Rang to station troops on either side of the granary city and wait.

sentences.zh: 其夕三鼓，世充兵果至，伯當先遇之，與戰，不利。

translations.literal: That night at the third watch Shichong's troops indeed arrived; Bodang met them first and fought, but fared poorly.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the third watch Shichong's troops arrived as expected. Bodang met them first and fought, but was driven back.

sentences.zh: 世充兵即陵城，總管魯儒拒卻之，伯當更收兵擊之，世充大敗，斬其驍將費青奴，士卒戰溺死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Shichong's troops immediately stormed the city walls; the commander Lu Ru repelled them; Bodang rallied his troops and struck again; Shichong was utterly defeated; his fierce general Fei Qingnu was beheaded; more than a thousand soldiers died in battle or drowning.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's men immediately assaulted the walls. Commander Lu Ru drove them back, and Bodang rallied his forces and struck again. Shichong was routed. His fierce general Fei Qingnu was beheaded, and more than a thousand soldiers were killed in battle or drowned.

sentences.zh: 世充屢與密戰，不勝，越王侗遣使勞之，世充訴以兵少，數戰疲弊；

translations.literal: Shichong fought Li Mi repeatedly without victory; Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent envoys to comfort him; Shichong complained that his troops were few and worn out from repeated battles;
translations.idiomatic: Shichong fought Li Mi again and again without winning. Prince of Yue Yang Tong sent envoys to encourage him. Shichong complained that his army was too small and exhausted from repeated battles;

sentences.zh: 侗以兵七萬益之。

translations.literal: Tong reinforced him with seventy thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong sent him seventy thousand more troops.

sentences.zh: 劉文靜等引兵東略地，取弘農郡，遂定新安以西。

translations.literal: Liu Wenjing and the others led troops east to seize territory, took Hongnong commandery, and then pacified all lands west of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wenjing and others led troops east to expand their holdings, captured Hongnong Commandery, and secured everything west of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，李淵遣雲陽令詹俊、武功縣正李仲袞徇巴、蜀，下之。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Li Yuan sent the magistrate of Yunyang Zhan Jun and the rectifier of Wugong Li Zhonggun to march against Ba and Shu and reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiachen, Li Yuan sent Zhan Jun, magistrate of Yunyang, and Li Zhonggun, rectifier of Wugong, to subdue Ba and Shu.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，方與帥張善安襲陷廬江郡，因渡江，歸林士弘於豫章；

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Zhang Shan'an, leader of Fangyu, raided and captured Lujiang commandery, then crossed the river and submitted to Lin Shihong at Yuzhang;
translations.idiomatic: On the day yisi, Zhang Shan'an, leader of Fangyu, raided and captured Lujiang Commandery, crossed the Yangzi, and submitted to Lin Shihong at Yuzhang;

sentences.zh: 士弘疑之，營於南塘上。

translations.literal: Shihong distrusted him and encamped on the south bank of the pond.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong distrusted him and made camp on the south bank of the pond.

sentences.zh: 善安恨之，襲破士弘，焚其郛郭而去，士弘徙居南康。

translations.literal: Shan'an bore a grudge, raided and defeated Shihong, burned his outer walls, and departed; Shihong moved his seat to Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan'an resented this, attacked and defeated Shihong, burned his outer defenses, and left. Shihong relocated to Nankang.

sentences.zh: 蕭銑遣其將蘇胡兒襲豫章，克之，士弘退保餘干。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian sent his general Su Hu'er to raid Yuzhang, took it, and Shihong withdrew to hold Yugan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian sent his general Su Hu'er to attack Yuzhang and captured it. Shihong withdrew to defend Yugan.
